title: Introduction: five vectors of FinTech disruption
summary: Financial Technologies (FinTech) such as mobile payments, blockchain and artificial intelligence are transforming financial services by powering faster payments and new forms of money in both developed and developing countries. FinTech is not only disrupting finance, we contend, but also contemporary politics by spurring divergent policy responses to cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and extending Big Tech’s societal reach and market power. FinTech is often presented as a catalyst for financial inclusion, but it can be a vehicle for criminality and corruption, and has intersected with the rise of right-wing populism. In this introduction, we identify five vectors of FinTech disruption covering (1) the international monetary order, (2) political authority, (3) security and trust, (4) inclusion, development and growth, and (5) financial governance. FinTech can be a force for good, but, if left unchecked, it has the potential to create a new monetary disorder.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility Moderates Green Accounting and Technological Innovation on Firm Value
summary: Firm value serves as an important measure of how investors assess a company’s performance and future prospects. As the business environment continues to evolve, environmental practices, technological innovation, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) have become increasingly important factors shaping these assessments. This study examines the effects of Green Accounting and Technological Innovation on Firm Value and investigates the moderating role of CSR among industrial and consumer non-cyclical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. A quantitative associative research design was employed using secondary data collected from annual reports, sustainability reports, PROPER reports, the Indonesia Stock Exchange, and official company websites. Using purposive sampling, the study obtained a sample of 37 companies, representing 185 observations. The data were analyzed through panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) using EViews 13. The findings show that Green Accounting has a negative effect on Firm Value, whereas Technological Innovation does not significantly affect Firm Value. CSR significantly moderates the relationship between Green Accounting and Firm Value by weakening the relationship, but does not significantly moderate the relationship between Technological Innovation and Firm Value. These results indicate that environmental practices, technological innovation, and CSR need to be managed and communicated in ways that clearly demonstrate their economic value and broader benefits to stakeholders.

title: When Does Fintech Translate into Corporate Green Innovation? Evidence on Governance Capacity, Capital Horizon, and Firm Heterogeneity
summary: Against the backdrop of intensifying global climate change and resource constraints, green innovation has become increasingly important to high-quality development. This study examines the effect of financial technology (fintech) development on corporate green innovation and the mechanisms through which this effect operates. Using a firm-level panel of 4,327 Chinese A-share listed companies from 2011 to 2024, comprising 34,842 firm-year observations, the analysis focuses on the mediating roles of financing constraints and digital transformation and the moderating roles of internal control quality and patient capital. The results show that fintech development significantly enhances corporate green innovation by alleviating financing constraints and facilitating digital transformation. The effect also exhibits meaningful heterogeneity across firms with different factor intensities and among “Specialized and Sophisticated” SMEs. In addition, stronger internal control and greater patient capital reinforce the positive effect of fintech on green innovation. These findings clarify the financial, technological, and governance channels through which fintech supports corporate green innovation and provide firm-level evidence for improving the coordination of digital finance and green development.

title: STATISTICAL ANALYSIS TO MEASURE THE ROLE OF ACCOUNTING DISCLOSURE ON CARBON NEUTRALITY IN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AUDIT COMMITTEES AND FINANCIAL REPORTING QUALITY
summary: This study investigates the relationship between audit committee characteristics and financial reporting quality (FRQ) among non-financial firms listed on the Saudi Exchange, while examining the moderating role of carbon neutrality disclosure.The analysis relies on a balanced panel dataset covering 160 firms over the period 2019-2024, resulting in 800 firm-year observations.Data are obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and the Mubasher database.Audit committee characteristics are measured through committee independence, size, and meeting frequency, whereas FRQ is proxied by accounting conservatism using the market-to-book ratio.Carbon neutrality disclosure is captured using a disclosure-based index reflecting the extent of firms' carbon-related and carbon-neutrality reporting.The empirical models control for firm size, leverage, profitability, and sector classification.Overall, the study highlights the importance of effective audit committee structures and sustainability transparency in shaping the quality of financial reporting, and it contributes to the governance and sustainability literature by providing evidence from the Saudi market.

title: Effect of Board Structure on Earnings Management in Listed Consumer Goods Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of board structure on earnings management among listed consumer goods companies in Nigeria. Drawing on agency and complementary governance theories, the study investigates how key board attributes; board size, board independence, board members’ financial expertise, multiple directorships, and board gender diversity individually and collectively influence earnings management. Using an ex-post facto research design and a quantitative approach, panel data were obtained from the annual reports of 16 firms over the period 2006–2022. The study employs Panel Corrected Standard Errors (PCSEs) regression to address cross-sectional dependence, heteroscedasticity, and serial correlation inherent in panel data. The findings reveal that board structure variables jointly have a significant effect on earnings management, confirming the importance of governance mechanisms in financial reporting quality. However, the results show mixed effects at the individual level where board size and board independence exhibit positive but statistically insignificant relationships with earnings management. In contrast, board members’ financial expertise has a positive and significant effect, suggesting that expertise could be associated with increased ability to manage earnings. Conversely, multiple directorships and board gender diversity demonstrate significant negative effects, indicating their effectiveness in reducing earnings manipulation. Thus, the study recommends that Consumer goods companies in Nigeria should as a matter of urgency prioritize enhancing the financial expertise of board members as well as promoting gender diversity on the board because the findings indicate that board members with financial expertise have a statistically significant impact on reducing earnings management. Therefore, management should actively seek to appoint directors with relevant financial qualifications and experience, particularly in accounting, auditing, or financial reporting to improve their ability to critically assess financial decisions, identify potential manipulations, and ensure transparency in financial reporting. Additionally, gender diversity has shown a highly significant negative impact on earnings management, implying that the management should implement policies to increase female representation on the board because a more gender-diverse board could introduce varied perspectives, enhance decision-making processes, and lead to better governance practices focused on reducing earnings manipulation.

title: Developing an Integrated Risk Governance Framework for Saudi Holding Companies in Support of Vision 2030
summary: Saudi holding companies are increasingly central to portfolio investment, sectoral diversification, localization, and large-scale transformation under Vision 2030. Their governance challenge is distinctive: while risks originate within individual subsidiaries, value destruction can propagate through shared financing, brands, digital infrastructure, suppliers, executives, and strategic dependencies at the group level. This review develops an integrated risk governance framework tailored to this multi-entity context. An integrative review approach synthesizes research on enterprise risk management, board governance, organizational resilience, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors, digital risk, supply-chain resilience, and Saudi corporate governance. The synthesis demonstrates that conventional subsidiary-by-subsidiary risk registers are inadequate when the parent company must understand risk concentration, contagion, correlated exposures, and strategic trade-offs across a portfolio. Effective governance therefore requires five interconnected capabilities: board-level risk direction and appetite; a group risk office capable of aggregating and challenging exposures; clearly retained subsidiary ownership of operational risks; independent assurance; and a continuous decision loop linking risk information to capital allocation, strategy, and learning. Saudi evidence further indicates that board structure, audit and sustainability mechanisms, institutional quality, disclosure, and investor expectations influence the credibility of governance arrangements. The proposed framework aligns these findings with Vision 2030 priorities by positioning risk governance as an infrastructure for disciplined growth rather than mere compliance. It provides a research agenda and practical design principles for holding-company boards, group chief risk officers, subsidiary leaders, regulators, and investors seeking resilience without sacrificing entrepreneurial autonomy.

title: Carbon lever and green gear: how firm-level carbon finance sparks green innovation efficiency in manufacturing
summary: In the face of mounting pressure on global initiatives to combat climate change, the question of how to capitalize on the opportunity presented by green transformation has become a pressing concern. Unlike the concept of green finance, carbon finance (CF) is a specific means dedicated to reducing greenhouse gases. Its essence lies in emerging financial tools based on strict technical accounting, with carbon emissions as the primary commodity and reliance on the financial market. Therefore, based on the data of A-share listed manufacturing enterprises from 2009 to 2023, this study constructs a carbon finance measurement at the firm level and explores the causal relationship between CF and the green innovation efficiency (GIE) of manufacturing enterprises. The findings indicate that: (1) Enterprises’ CF can boost the GIE. High-tech manufacturing companies, as well as those in the mature and declining stages, exhibit this boosting influence in particular. (2) The development of CF can enhance the GIE of enterprises through two main channels: increasing the proportion of senior executives with environmental backgrounds and improving the short-term debt-paying ability of enterprises. (3) The impact of CF is moderated both positively and negatively by the degree of digital integration (Dig) and financing constraints (Sa). The level of Dig and Sa play a positive and negative moderation role in the impact of carbon finance. The results provide a reference for the application of carbon financial tools in the entity economy from a micro perspective.

title: Firm size as a boundary condition for CSR value creation: evidence from multi-African capital markets
summary: This study examines whether firm size functions as a boundary condition shaping the association between corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure and firm value in African capital markets, drawing on flexibility theory and the resource-based view (RBV) to develop competing predictions about the direction of size moderation. A balanced panel of listed firms across South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, and Ghana over a decade is analysed using two-way fixed-effects regression, with firm size operationalised through continuous, market-based, and categorical specifications, and firm value captured through both market-based (Tobin’s Q) and accounting-based (Economic Value Added) measures. Subgroup regressions, lagged specifications, and alternative dependent variable tests provide complementary robustness evidence. The findings indicate that the CSR-value association is concentrated among smaller listed firms in several, though not all, specifications, offering qualified rather than conclusive support for flexibility theory over the resource-based view. The accounting-based evidence is more consistent with a negative size moderation pattern than the market-based interaction evidence. The study contributes multi-country African panel evidence to the CSR boundary conditions literature and offers cautious theoretical and practical implications for managers, investors, and regulators operating across Africa’s heterogeneous capital markets.

title: AI AND BIG DATA ANALYTICS FOR LOCAL CONTENT OPTIMIZATION IN SAUDI INDUSTRIAL SUPPLY CHAINS
summary: Saudi Arabias industrial transformation under Vision 2030 increasingly depends on the ability of public and private organizations to convert local-content objectives into efficient, measurable and commercially sustainable supply - chain decisions. Conventional local - content programs frequently rely on static supplier lists, periodic procurement reports and manual category assessments, making it difficult to respond to rapid changes in demand, supplier capability, cost, technology and supply risk. This paper develops an artificial intelligence (AI) and big-data analytics framework for optimizing local content across Saudi industrial supply chains. Using a structured review and conceptual framework methodology, the study integrates recent literature on AI-enabled supply chains, big-data analytics, Industry 4.0, supplier development and supply-chain resilience with official Saudi Vision 2030 and merchandise-trade evidence. The proposed framework contains six decision modules: spend intelligence, demand forecasting, supplier-capability analytics, localization opportunity prediction, supply-risk analytics and local-content performance optimization.

title: Environmental sustainability meets digital transformation: Dilemmas and new directions
summary: The academic publishing industry faces a strategic crossroads where environmental sustainability imperatives intersect with digital transformation opportunities. This situation creates challenges that extend beyond simple print-to-digital migration. Drawing on interviews with 10 major publishers, our case shows that effective sustainability strategies rely on hybrid models rather than binary choices. While digital formats reduce carbon emissions, they introduce new complexities in measurement, supply chain governance, and market acceptance. Findings reveal that most of the industry’s carbon footprint originates not from publishers’ own operations but from upstream supplier activities such as paper production, printing, and digital infrastructure, areas over which publishers exert limited direct influence. These indirect emissions dominate both print and digital life cycles yet remain difficult to quantify due to complex global supply chains, variable energy sources, and evolving ICT technologies. Addressing this requires new capabilities in supplier management, cultural change, and compliance with varied regulatory regimes. Five strategic priorities emerge: optimizing hybrid models, orchestrating supply chains, building measurement frameworks, transforming professional markets, and navigating regional regulations. These insights challenge simplistic narratives of digital benefits and offer guidance for balancing innovation with environmental responsibility.

title: Digitalization trends in EU corporate law and corporate governance
summary: The article examines the current trends in the digitalization of company law and corporate governance in the European Union and determines their significance for the further development of Ukraine’s national company law within the context of European integration. The relevance of the study is caused the rapid development of digital technologies and the need to modernize the mechanisms for the state registration of legal entities, digitalize corporate procedures, ensure the transparency of corporate information, and enhance the effective functioning of the EU internal market. Particular attention is paid to the analysis of recent legislative developments aimed at establishing a unified European digital corporate environment based on the mutual recognition of data contained in national business registers, the use of electronic identification, and digital instruments for interaction between the competent authorities of the Member States. The paper analyses the evolution of the legal framework governing the digitalization of EU company law, with particular emphasis on the provisions of Directive (EU) 2019/1151 and Directive (EU) 2025/25. It explores the functioning of the Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS), the “once-only principle”, electronic company registration mechanisms, the use of standard templates for instruments of constitution, the Digital EU Power of Attorney, and the EU Company Certificate. Their role in enhancing the reliability of corporate information, simplifying administrative procedures, ensuring corporate transparency, and facilitating cross-border interaction among business entities is examined. The study substantiates that the current stage of the digitalization of company law is characterized by a transition from the digitalization of individual administrative procedures to the establishment of a comprehensive and integrated system of electronic interaction between the corporate registers of the EU Member States. At the same time, the principal challenges of further digital transformation are identified, including the uneven level of digitalization among Member States, the need to ensure the cross-border interoperability of digital systems, the guarantee of legal certainty, the authenticity of electronic documents, and the adequate protection of digital corporate data. The article concludes that the experience of the European Union is of paramount practical importance for the modernization of Ukrainian company law and the improvement of digital corporate governance mechanisms in the process of harmonizing national legislation with the EU acquis.

title: Digital Transformation in Management Accounting: Drivers, Barriers and Evidence from Saudi Arabia
summary: Purpose: This study examines how organisational drivers and implementation barriers shape digital transformation in management accounting across Saudi organisations. It addresses the limited empirical evidence on the simultaneous influence of enabling and constraining conditions within an emerging-market management accounting context. Design/Methodology/Approach: Survey data were collected from 190 management accounting and finance professionals in Saudi organisations and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The model estimates the effects of a four-item Drivers construct (management support, digital strategy, employee motivation and resource readiness) and a four-item Barriers construct (resistance to change, digital skills gaps, systems-integration difficulties and security/privacy/regulatory concerns) on a four-item Digital Transformation construct. Measurement reliability and validity, structural paths, collinearity and effect sizes were assessed, followed by a supplementary robustness model controlling for organisation size, organisation type and respondent experience. Findings: Drivers exert a significant positive effect on digital transformation (β = 0.498, p < 0.001), whereas Barriers exert a significant negative effect (β = −0.431, p < 0.001). The model explains 54.2% of the variance in digital transformation (R² = 0.542). Both predictors make substantial incremental contributions (f² = 0.506 and 0.381, respectively), and collinearity is low (VIF = 1.068). The focal relationships remain stable after controlling for organisation size, organisation type and respondent experience (Drivers β = 0.493; Barriers β = −0.435; both p < 0.001). Implications/Originality/Value: The study moves beyond treating digital transformation as a purely technological initiative by modelling enabling capabilities and implementation frictions simultaneously within management accounting. It provides evidence from Saudi organisations showing that digital transformation depends on strengthening organisational readiness while reducing human and systems-related constraints, and it uses the TOE framework as a contextual organising lens rather than as a rigid three-dimensional measurement structure.

title: Financing Green Supply Chain Management: Key Components for Building Construction Project Delivery in South-East Nigeria
summary: The buildings and construction sector accounted for approximately 37% of global CO₂ emissions in 2023, creating an urgent need for Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) in construction. This study develops a GSCM framework for building construction project delivery in South-East Nigeria by identifying and ranking key GSCM components. A structured questionnaire was administered to 890 construction professionals across five states, with 844 valid responses analysed using the Relative Importance Index (RII). The findings reveal five GSCM dimensions: environmental, economic, social/human, operational/technological, and regulatory/policy/strategic. The highest-ranked components were Resource Conservation (ENV, RII = 0.791), Cost-effectiveness of Green Materials (ECO, RII = 0.791), Public Awareness (SOC, RII = 0.724), Green Innovation (OP, RII = 0.796), and International Standards Compliance (RP, RII = 0.746). The study concludes that GSCM in building construction is multidimensional, requiring coordinated attention to environmental, economic, social, operational, and regulatory factors. The framework provides a context-specific evidence base for policymakers, construction professionals, and stakeholders seeking to strengthen sustainable supply-chain practices in South-East Nigeria.

title: Supply chain digitization and cost of equity capital: Evidence from China
summary: Supply chain management, which can integrate upstream and downstream resources, has been becoming the core path for manufacturing to build sustainable competitive advantages. To optimize supply chain management, China introduced pilot policies for supply chain innovation and application (SCIA) in 2018. Employing a sample of Chinese A-share listed enterprises from 2012 to 2020, we use the difference-in-difference (DID) method to examine the influence of SCIA pilot policy on the cost of equity capital(COEC). The results show that (1) Supply chain(SC) digitization can greatly reduce COEC, but there is a time-lag effect. (2) The mechanism analysis shows that SC digitization reduces COEC by improving corporate innovation capacity and information quality. (3) Heterogeneity analysis shows that the reduction effect of SC digitization on COEC is more significant in firms with lower SC digitization and high-tech firms.

title: Policy coordination of public data openness and supercomputing center for agricultural chain resilience
summary: Strengthening agricultural supply chain resilience is critical for safeguarding food security and promoting high-quality agricultural development in the face of escalating external shocks, including climate extremes, market volatility, and geopolitical uncertainties. Although public data openness and supercomputing infrastructure represent critical pillars of digital transformation, how their coordinated deployment enhances agricultural resilience remains both theoretically underdeveloped and empirically underexamined. Using provincial panel data from 31 Chinese provinces over 2011–2024, we exploit the staggered rollout of public data platforms and supercomputing centers as quasi-natural experiments, constructing a synergistic difference-in-differences (DID) model to isolate their coordinated policy effects. The causal identification is further fortified using event-study parallel trend tests, placebo simulations, propensity score matching (PSM-DID), and double/debiased machine learning (DDML). Our baseline estimates demonstrate that policy synergy between public data openness and supercomputing infrastructure substantially enhances agricultural supply chain resilience, with effects remaining robust across multiple specifications and economically significant. Mechanistic analysis reveals two primary transmission channels through which policy synergy strengthens resilience: (i) industrial structure rationalization, and (ii) agricultural electrification enhancement. Specifically, policy coordination (1) reduces informational barriers between agricultural and related industries, (2) facilitates optimal factor reallocation across sectors, and (3) accelerates the adoption of electricity-intensive precision agriculture technologies. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that policy effectiveness is substantially greater in central and western regions (coefficient ~0.089) compared to eastern regions (coefficient ~0.036), suggesting a ‘technology compensation effect’ whereby digital infrastructure offsets traditional regional disparities. Policy effects remain robustly positive across both major grain-producing and grain-consuming zones, indicating broad applicability. By unpacking the complementary and sequential dynamics between data factors and computing capacity, this study moves beyond the traditional “black box” treatment of the digital economy, providing critical policy insights for the coordinated deployment of digital public goods to secure modern food systems.

title: Policy Translation under Audit: Vice Principals and the Governing of Digital Transformation in Vietnamese Primary Schools
summary: Aim. This article examines how vice principals in Vietnamese primary schools translate digital transformation mandates into evidence-informed implementation practice. It argues that policy effects depend not only on formal mandates or technological tools, but also on how school leaders interpret and adapt these expectations in local school contexts. Methods. Drawing on Bakhtin’s distinction between authoritative discourse and internally persuasive discourse, the study approaches implementation as a process of policy translation. A qualitative, retrospective narrative case-based design was used. Three vice principals from public primary schools in northern Vietnam, recognised for technology-related initiatives, were purposively selected as information-rich cases. Data were generated through retrospective semi-structured interviews and supplemented by implementation-related artefacts. Results. Three recurring translation mechanisms were identified: reframing mandates as practical pedagogical and organisational problems; mobilising evidence to justify and sustain digital practices; and aligning implementation with school capacity, teacher readiness, and professional culture. Conclusions. The findings suggest that digital transformation is more likely to be sustained when policy is translated into context-sensitive routines rather than enacted primarily as formal compliance. Practical implications. The findings indicate the need for clearer role definition, stronger implementation support, and evidence frameworks that balance improvement aims with documentation requirements.

title: A Curated Corpus of Climate Finance Literature, 1990–2024
summary: This data paper presents a curated, multilingual corpus of 33,344 works on climate finance published between 1990 and 2024. The dataset is assembled from 8 complementary sources that combine academic databases with a selected layer of institutional reports and key documents (1.4% of the corpus), adding institutional vocabulary and negotiation records absent from academic indexes. A multilingual retrieval strategy based on an eight-language keyword taxonomy is used to capture relevant works across linguistic contexts, while a reproducible pipeline integrates deduplication, metadata harmonisation, and quality filtering. English accounts for 93.8% of the refined works. The corpus includes a citation network derived from Crossref and OpenAlex, as well as embeddings pre-computed by a multilingual sentence-transformer.

title: Human–AI symbiosis for resilient supply chains: a Delphi-fuzzy cognitive mapping analysis of an Indian textile sector
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can augment rather than replace human decision-making in human-centric supply chains, and how this synergy enhances supply chain flexibility (SCF) and supply chain resilience (SCR), using a textile sector in North India as the real-world context. Design/methodology/approach The study is conducted in two phases. The first phase focuses on identifying and prioritizing the relevant AI-related and human-centric factors for the study, which is addressed through an exhaustive literature review for identification and then the Delphi method to prioritize them. The second phase focuses on modeling the relationship between these factors using fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) approach. Expert inputs are used to construct the causal structure and analyze the strength of interconnections. By modeling bidirectional and nonlinear relationships rather than assuming static, unidirectional causality, this method captures feedback dynamics, which conventional linear techniques cannot represent. Findings The results show that human-centric factors particularly human–AI augmentation, human–machine collaboration and workforce preparedness play a central role in translating AI capabilities into SCF and SCR. AI-related factors primarily act as drivers, while supply chain outcomes materialize through these human-centric mechanisms. Originality/value This study offers a mechanism-based explanation of AI-enabled supply chain performance and employs FCM to capture complex interrelationships within a sociotechnical system.

title: THE IMPACT OF ESG PRACTICES ON SUSTAINABLE QUALITY PERFORMANCE AND COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE: EVIDENCE FROM CHINA'S GREEN HOTEL INDUSTRY
summary: This study examines how environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices affect competitive advantage, with a focus on the mediating role of consumer purchase intention in hospitality.Using a quantitative approach, survey data from 350 respondents were analysed via Smart PLS structural equation modelling.Results reveal that ESG practices exert direct positive effects on competitive advantage and consumer purchase intention.Purchase intention significantly mediates the ESG-competitive advantage relationship.Consumer behaviour serves as a vital channel connecting corporate social responsibility to market performance.Strong purchase intention boosts competitive advantage, highlighting the need for effective ESG communication aligned with consumer values.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Financial Services: Emerging Business Models, Opportunities and Challenges
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain and digital payment technologies is transforming the structure and functioning of modern commerce. The financial services sector is one of the most technology-intensive sectors, where digital transformation has changed traditional banking, payment systems, lending, investment management, insurance and customer relationship management. Artificial Intelligence has emerged as a particularly important technology because of its ability to analyse large volumes of structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, automate decisions and provide personalised services.This chapter examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in transforming financial services and creating emerging business models. It discusses major applications of AI in banking and finance, including fraud detection, credit assessment, customer service, personalised financial products, risk management, regulatory compliance, investment management and digital payments. The chapter also examines emerging models such as AI-powered banking, embedded finance, Banking-as-a-Service, FinTech platforms, intelligent digital lending and AI-enabled financial ecosystems. At the same time, the adoption of AI introduces challenges related to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, model risk, technological dependency and regulatory compliance. The chapter proposes a responsible AI adoption framework based on governance, data quality, transparency, human oversight, cybersecurity and continuous monitoring. The discussion is particularly relevant to emerging markets such as India, where digital public infrastructure and FinTech innovation are rapidly changing the financial ecosystem.

title: Economic Resilience in AI-Driven FinTech, ESG Integration, and Sustainable Financial Systems: A Human-Centered Approach
summary: This paper quantitatively examines employees’ perceptions of the relationships among AI-driven Financial Technology (FinTech), Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) integration, Human-Centered Factors, and Economic Resilience in banks and FinTech firms in Jordan. Rather than using objective organizational or macroeconomic indicators, the study measures respondents’ perceptions of AI-driven financial technologies, ESG-oriented practices, human-centered considerations, and their organizations’ ability to withstand, adapt to, and recover from economic and financial disruptions. An integrated framework combining technological, sustainability, and human-centered dimensions was developed to examine these relationships. Data from 353 usable questionnaires were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrated significant positive associations between AI-driven FinTech and both ESG Integration and Economic Resilience. ESG Integration significantly mediated the association between AI-driven FinTech and Economic Resilience, while Human-Centered Factors were positively associated with AI-driven FinTech and significantly moderated the association between AI-driven FinTech and Economic Resilience. The model explained 65% of the variance in Economic Resilience (R2 = 0.65). The findings contribute to the digital finance literature by integrating technological, sustainability, and human-centered dimensions while emphasizing the organizational and perceptual context of the evidence. Given the cross-sectional nature of the study and the perceptual measures used, the findings should be interpreted as associations within the participating organizations rather than as evidence of causal effects or national economic or financial-system resilience.

title: The Influence of Digital Transformation on GDP Growth: Insights from BRICS Economies
summary: The Influence of Digital Transformation on GDP Growth: Insights from BRICS Economies Dr. Ayush Kumar* Laxmi Shanker Gupta** This paper examines the impact of digital transformation on GDP growth in BRICS economies (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa). As digital technologies—such as the internet, mobile networks, artificial intelligence, and fintech—rapidly expand, they reshape industries and spur economic development. title: Ефективність податкового контролю в умовах цифровізації економіки: виклики та можливості
summary: The paper provides a comprehensive study of the processes of digitalization of the economy and tax system of Ukraine. Based on the analysis, the importance of digitalization as a key factor in increasing the competitiveness of the state, the efficiency of business processes, and ensuring sustainable economic development is substantiated. The evolution of the digital economy from the early stages of automation to the current stage associated with the use of the latest digital technologies is examined. It is determined that the digitalization of the economy creates the conditions for the development of new business models, increased labor productivity, and reduced transaction costs. The paper analyzes the main directions of the implementation of the state policy of digital transformation, in particular Ukraine’s participation in the EU programs “Digital Europe,” “EU4Digital,” and “EU4PFM,” which are aimed at developing digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and improving the efficiency of public finance management. Based on the analysis, it was determined that the digitization of the tax system is one of the priority areas of the digital economy, as it ensures transparency, reliability, and controllability of financial flows. Particular attention is paid to the study of electronic auditing as a tool for the digital transformation of tax control. The essence and purpose of electronic auditing of taxpayers has been substantiated, its key stages and advantages over traditional forms of auditing have been identified. It has been established that one of the tools of e-audit is the use of the standard tax audit file SAF-T. The main challenges accompanying the introduction of electronic auditing in Ukraine have been identified: insufficient development of IT infrastructure, gaps in regulatory and legal regulation, risks associated with the protection of tax information. Overcoming these barriers requires a systematic approach and coordination between government agencies, businesses, and international partners.

title: Do female directors promote corporate social responsibility during the post-mandate period? Evidence from India and China
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether female directors promote corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the post-mandate period and how this effect varies between family and non-family firms in India and China. Design/methodology/approach The authors analyse 9,453 firm-year observations from 1,532 Indian firms and 2,421 firm-year observations from 450 Chinese firms over 2010–2019 using fixed-effects panel regressions, difference-in-differences and instrumental variable approaches. Findings The authors find that increased board gender diversity relates with higher CSR spending, with stronger benefits following the implementation of board gender quotas in India. The increase of CSR in the post-mandate period is in line with reputational and monitoring incentives for female directors facing increased regulatory and stakeholder scrutiny. The positive relationship between female directors and CSR is stronger in family businesses, implying that family-related socioemotional wealth considerations strengthen stakeholder-oriented CSR. The relationship between gender diversity and CSR differs depending on the type of CSR activities. The findings indicate that women directors in India are mainly related with community CSR, whereas in China they are more strongly associated with environmental CSR, reflecting differences in stakeholder engagement and regulation emphasis. Overall, findings suggest that gender mandates can serve as an effective governance instrument for reshaping both the extent and composition of CSR. Originality/value The authors show that reputational incentives significantly impact the women director’s decision to encourage CSR activities. We also find that to maintain their reputations and comply with the regulations, women directors of highly profitable firms promote CSR activities in India and China.

title: Cross-industry Technological Information Spillovers through Analyst Networks
summary: Do equity analysts transmit technological information across industries? I show that, through within-brokerage networks, analysts acquire technological knowledge from firms in other industries and apply it to the firms they cover. I measure these spillovers using technological connectedness (TC), based on patent-distribution similarity between a focal firm and firms covered by colleagues in other industries. Using brokerage M&As as quasi-exogenous shocks to analyst networks, I show that higher-TC analysts issue more accurate earnings forecasts. At the firm level, high-TC analysts improve innovation quality by curbing low-impact patenting. Coverage by high-TC analysts also attenuates technology momentum in stock returns.

title: Feedback-enabled digital twin and explainable artificial intelligence framework for predictive resilience and adaptive decision-making in disrupted supply chains
summary: Supply-chain disruptions are increasingly difficult to manage with conventional monitor–respond–recover approaches because they provide limited early-warning, explanation, uncertainty assessment and adaptive recovery support. This study developed a feedback-enabled digital twin and explainable artificial intelligence framework for predictive resilience and adaptive decision-making in disrupted supply chains. A quantitative modelling, simulation and multi-objective optimization design was applied to a hybrid dataset containing 3,500 de-identified operational shipment records from CarryGo Logistics Company, Awka, Nigeria, and 1,500 simulation-generated rare-disruption observations. The data were divided into 3,500 training, 750 validation and 750 testing observations, with validation and testing conducted entirely on operational records. Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM and Bayesian Neural Network models were evaluated, while 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation, SHAP analysis and normalized multi-objective optimization supported uncertainty assessment, explanation and recovery selection. Random Forest achieved 0.79 accuracy, 0.61 precision, 0.99 recall, 0.75 F1 and 0.85 AUC, whereas XGBoost achieved 0.62 precision, 0.86 recall, 0.85 AUC and the lowest MAE of 0.27. The framework classified 353 normal, 61 watch, 333 warning and 3 critical states. Disruption severity increased from 22% at supplier failure to 83% customer-service loss across the simulated network. Supplier reliability and lead time contributed 41.49 and 39.97% of disruption risk, respectively. Inventory redistribution ranked first under equal weights with J = 0.26 and remained preferred under service and risk priorities, while supplier switching became optimal under cost and delay priorities. The framework demonstrates company-level operational utility for transparent, uncertainty-aware and feedback-enabled supply-chain resilience, while wider multi-company validation remains necessary.

title: Does Green Credit Policy Enhance Firms’ Green Total Factor Productivity? Evidence from China
summary: Green finance is a crucial tool for facilitating environmental governance. This paper uses China’s issuance of the Green Credit Guidelines as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a difference-in-differences strategy to examine the impact of green credit policies on firms’ green total factor productivity (GTFP). The results show that green credit policies significantly enhance firms’ GTFP. Decomposing GTFP reveals that green credit primarily enhances firms’ green productivity via green technological progress rather than green efficiency change. Further analysis suggests that green credit improves GTFP through two main channels: promoting green innovation and reducing agency costs. Heterogeneity tests demonstrate that the positive effects are more pronounced for state-owned enterprises, large-scale firms, and firms in heavily polluting industries. This paper provides micro-level empirical evidence on the productivity effects of green credit and offers insights for policymakers seeking to promote firms’ green transformation through financial instruments.

title: Blockchain enabled anti-counterfeiting framework for luxury supply chain system
summary: Blockchain technology is growing rapidly with an increase in demand for efficient and transparent supply-chain management systems, especially for the luxury goods industry. Annual counterfeit losses account for approximately $30 billion dollars due to the lack of effective systems to combat fraud, forgery and malicious attacks in the supply-chain system. Existing systems lack effective anti-counterfeiting measures, exhibit fragmented data architectures and depend on centralised entities for decision-making. As a key solution to the current challenges in the luxury goods supply chain, we propose a novel Blockchain framework for Luxury Goods Authentication and Supply Chain Transparency (BLAST). The system is designed to address counterfeiting, privacy-preserving authentication and ensure end-to-end product traceability. It consists of decentralised identity consensus with cryptographic verification mechanism, dynamic role-based access control to prevent unauthorised access into the system, adaptive trust engine and reputation mechanism for stakeholder and consumer incentive and structured product lifecycle tracking for efficient traceability and transparency. Complete provenance history of a product from its manufacturing to resale is retrieved by scanning a QR code that is cryptographically bound to the product’s Physical Unclonable Function (PUF). Experimental results and cost analysis validate the efficiency of the proposed system over existing approaches.

title: ESG Rating Divergence and Corporate Debt Structure: Evidence from China
summary: Against the backdrop of rising global debt risks and increasing attention to debt-structure optimization, this study examines how ESG rating divergence relates to corporate debt structure. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2015 to 2023, we find that ESG rating divergence is associated with higher debt concentration and lower debt-type diversity. It is also linked to a lower share of interest-bearing liabilities and a higher share of non-interest-bearing liabilities. Mechanism analyses indicate that debt financing costs and cash flow volatility serve as important channels, as they restrict firms’ access to stable external financing. Additional analyses reveal that these effects are amplified when regional financial development is limited, external media attention is low, ESG reports are not externally assured, and managerial short-termism is more severe. In addition, rating divergence across the three ESG pillars is significantly related to debt-structure adjustments. By linking ESG rating divergence to firms’ debt financing choices, this study extends the ESG finance literature and offers practical implications for corporate financing decisions, investor risk assessment, and ESG rating regulation.

title: Risk mitigation in oil and gas supply chain: a systematic literature review
summary: The oil and gas (O&G) industry faces significant risks across its supply chain. These include geopolitical, operational, and environmental challenges. Mitigating these risks is important to ensure safety, efficiency, and resilience in the global energy systems. This study conducts a systematic literature review of over 150 peer-reviewed articles published between 2011 and 2025 to examine how supply chain risks in the O&G industry are identified, assessed, and mitigated. Following a transparent screening and selection process, a thematic analysis is applied to synthesize evidence on risk drivers, enabling capabilities, and mitigation strategies. The review addresses four research questions concerning dominant risk categories, mitigation practices, emerging technologies and methodologies, and firm-level responses to supply chain disruptions. The study’s main contribution is the development of an integrated risk mitigation framework that explains how enabling capabilities mediate between risk drivers and mitigation outcomes, offering both theoretical insights and practical guidance for risk management in the oil and gas supply chain (O&GSC). The review proposes further empirical studies. It offers a foundation for developing more robust, context-specific mitigation frameworks.

title: The Effect of Good Corporate Governance on Firm Value, with Profitability as A Mediator, in Companies in The Non-Cyclical Consumer Sector Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange for The Period 2022–2024
summary: This study evaluated the effect of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) on financial performance and firm value among consumer non-cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2024 period, while also examining the mediating role of financial performance. Employing a quantitative research design with a purposive sampling method, the study used a sample of 44 companies, resulting in 100 observations. The empirical data were analyzed using multiple linear regression, path analysis, and the Sobel test with SPSS version 27. The findings showed that Good Corporate Governance (GCG) components had varying effects on profitability and firm value. Independent commissioners positively influenced profitability, whereas audit committee size negatively affected profitability, and board size had no statistically significant effect. Board size and audit committee size negatively affected firm value, while independent commissioners did not have a statistically significant effect on firm value. Profitability positively influenced firm value and successfully mediated the effects of independent commissioners and audit committee size; however, it did not mediate the relationship between board size and firm value. Board size had the highest mean value, indicating that it was the most dominant governance factor associated with profitability and firm value.

title: Pengaruh Literasi Keuangan dan Edukasi Pasar Modal terhadap Keputusan Berinvestasi di Galeri Investasi Syariah Studi pada Mahasiswa FEBI UIN STS Jambi
summary: The development of the digital economy has increased public awareness of the importance of investment as a means of achieving long-term financial goals. This study aims to analyze the influence of financial literacy and capital market education on students' investment decisions at the Sharia Investment Gallery of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business, Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin State Islamic University of Jambi. This research employed a quantitative method, with data collected through questionnaires and analyzed using statistical techniques. The results indicate that financial literacy and capital market education have a positive and significant effect on students' investment decisions, both partially and simultaneously. These findings suggest that higher levels of financial literacy and better understanding of the capital market lead to more effective investment decisions among students. Therefore, enhancing financial literacy and capital market education is essential to support sound investment decision-making among university students.

title: Digital Transformation of Indian Commerce and the Changing World of Work: A Conceptual Review of Business, Employment and Workforce Capability
summary: This conceptual review examines how digital transformation is reshaping Indian commerce and the world of work that sustains it. Adopting an integrative literature review design, the study synthesises 30 scholarly and institutional sources, comprising foundational theory on technology and organisations, recent evidence on automation and artificial intelligence, and India-focused research and official reports on digitalisation, employment, informality and leadership, through thematic analysis. Four themes emerge: the digitalisation of commercial activity, the recomposition of employment, the centrality of workforce capability and leadership, and the risk of a widening divide between the organised economy and traditional and unorganised sectors. Official estimates place India's digital economy at 11.74% of national income in 2022-23, with a projected share of nearly one-fifth by 2029-30, which underlines the scale of the shift. The synthesis indicates that the employment effects of digitalisation are compositional and not uniformly negative, that returns to digital investment depend on complementary human and organisational capabilities, and that the informal workforce, including handloom producers, construction labour and migrant workers, remains largely outside the digital dividend. The paper integrates these insights into a Digital Commerce–Work–Capability framework and advances five research propositions for empirical testing. It offers practical guidance for business managers, educational institutions and policymakers seeking inclusive digital growth.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility dan Enterprise Risk Management Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di BEI Tahun 2021-2024
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) terhadap nilai perusahaan manufaktur yang tercatat di Bursa Efek Indonesia sepanjang periode 2021–2024. Dengan pendekatan kuantitatif, penelitian ini mengolah data sekunder dari laporan tahunan dan laporan tahunan sebanyak 203 observasi. Pengungkapan CSR diukur melalui Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index (CSRDI) berdasarkan GRI Standards 2021, sedangkan pengungkapan ERM diukur melalui Enterprise Risk Management Disclosure Index (ERMDI) yang mengacu pada COSO Framework . Nilai perusahaan diproksikan dengan rasio Price to Book Value (PBV), dan pengujian data dilakukan melalui regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa CSR berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap nilai perusahaan semakin tinggi jarak CSR, semakin besar peningkatan nilai perusahaan yang terjadi. Sebaliknya, ERM berpengaruh negatif signifikan, yang mengindikasikan bahwa pengungkapan ERM belum menjadi pertimbangan utama investor dalam menilai perusahaan manufaktur. Temuan ini menegaskan relevansi Stakeholder Theory dalam menjelaskan peran CSR sebagai instrumen legitimasi sosial dan reputasi, sekaligus menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas ERM sangat bergantung pada kualitas implementasi dan persepsi pemangku kepentingan .

title: Determinants influencing digital twin adoption decision in food supply chains
summary: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly recognised as a promising solution for food supply chains (FSCs). However, existing DT research has focused mainly on conceptual development, technical applications, and pilot implementations, providing limited empirical evidence on the determinants influencing firms’ adoption decisions. Thus, this study examines the determinants of DT adoption decisions in FSCs. Drawing on Diffusion of Innovation theory and the technology–organisation–environment (TOE) framework, the study develops a research model explaining how TOE factors shape firms’ adoption decisions. Survey data from 260 respondents in food and technology-related firms across Western economies are analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results show that compatibility, technology readiness, top management support, competitive pressure, and market uncertainty significantly influence the DT adoption decision, while complexity negatively affects adoption. Findings indicate that the DT adoption decision in FSCs is shaped not only by perceived technological characteristics but also by organisational support and external environmental pressures.

title: GENDER DIVERSITY AND FINANCIAL REPORTING QUALITY OF LISTED NON- FINANCIAL FIRMS IN NIGERIA: THE MODERATING ROLE OF DIGITAL GOVERNANCE
summary: Abstract This study examines the effect of gender diversity on financial reporting quality of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria, and the moderating role of digital governance. Specifically, it tests the influence of female directors’ educational qualifications and IT expertise on absolute discretionary accruals, and whether digital governance alters these relationships. Motivated by persistent concerns over earnings management and the increasing role of technology in corporate oversight, the study uses ex post facto design. Secondary data were obtained from the annual reports of 38 firms on the Nigerian Exchange Group for 2016–2025. Financial reporting quality was measured with absolute discretionary accruals. Descriptive statistics, correlation, and panel regression with robust standard errors were applied. Results show that female directors’ education has a positive but insignificant effect on reporting quality. Female IT expertise has a positive and significant effect on discretionary accruals, suggesting lower reporting quality. However, digital governance significantly moderates the IT expertise–reporting quality link, weakening the adverse effect. The moderation for education is not significant. The study concludes that the impact of gender diversity is attribute-specific and contingent on digital governance. It recommends that firms strengthen digital governance and integrate female IT directors into financial oversight to improve reporting quality. JEL Classification: G34, M41, G32, O55

title: THE ROLE OF SMALL AND MEDIUM BUSINESSES IN THE ESG TRANSFORMATION OF REGIONAL ECONOMY
summary: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) play a key role in achieving regional development goals, yet their potential for ESG transformation remains understudied. The objective of this study is to determine the contribution of SMEs to regional socioeconomic stability and assess their support for ESG principles for decision makers. The research methodology includes an analysis of rating data (EKG-region, ESG rankings), materials from the Ministry of Economic Development of the Russian Federation and the National Research Association (NRA), as well as a case study of Russian projects in the field of responsible consumption and recycling. The study's novelty lies in its comparative approach to macrostatistics and project data, which for the first time reveal typical barriers for Russian SMEs. The results confirm the sector's significant contribution to employment and demonstrate a high level of readiness for ESG transformation. The key barriers to scaling were identified as the lack of industrial production, technological dependence, and the need to adapt business models to local conditions. The findings substantiate the need for institutional support for SMEs in green supply chains. The practical ingenuity of the study lies in its systematization of success factors and their resolution, which allows for the development of targeted recommendations for regional policy.

title: THE EVOLUTION OF GLOBAL FINANCIAL REPORTING: STRATEGIC IMPLICATIONS OF IFRS INTEGRATION IN 2026
summary: This article examines contemporary issues in international financial reporting, with particular attention to the transition to IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements, the move by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) to establish global sustainability disclosure requirements, and the continuing debate over the extent to which accounting standards can be principles-based rather than rules-based. Using Uzbekistan as an illustrative emerging-market case, the paper combines accounting theory, institutional theory and empirical evidence on IFRS adoption to explain both the anticipated benefits of IFRS 18 (greater transparency, comparability and reduced information asymmetry) and the institutional constraints that may limit its impact, including enforcement capacity, professional skills and digital infrastructure. The article closes with strategic implications for regulators, preparers, auditors, educators and investors.

title: Analysis of Stock Investment Decisions in Generation Z in the Capital Market
summary: This study aims to examine the influence of financial literacy, investment motivation, and information technology on the investment interest of Generation Z in the Capital Market, focusing on students of the Management Study Program at Nahdlatul Ulama University of North Sumatra (UNUSU). This research employed a quantitative approach involving 89 students selected through saturated sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires with a Likert scale and analyzed through multiple linear regression using SPSS. Hypothesis testing was conducted using the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The findings indicate that financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on investment interest, while investment motivation has no significant effect. Meanwhile, information technology has a positive and significant effect on investment interest. Simultaneously, financial literacy, investment motivation, and information technology have a positive and significant effect on Generation Z’s investment interest in the Capital Market. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.778 indicates that the three independent variables explain 77.8% of the variation in investment interest, while the remaining 22.2% is influenced by other factors outside the study. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening financial literacy and utilizing information technology to encourage UNUSU students’ interest in investing in the Capital Market.

title: Integration of the performance of the internal and external auditor and its reflection in the quality of the audit in accordance with International Standard on Auditing (610)
summary: This research aims to study the integration of the performance of internal and external auditors and its impact on the quality of the audit process, in light of International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 610, which governs the use of internal auditors' work by external auditors. The importance of this research stems from the vital role that both internal and external auditing play in enhancing the reliability of financial reports and achieving transparency, especially in today's complex and increasingly risky business environment. The research adopted a descriptive-analytical approach by reviewing the theoretical framework of the integration concept between internal and external auditing, analyzing the nature of the relationship between them, and their impact on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the audit process. The practical aspect included analyzing the research sample data using statistical tools to measure the level of integration and its impact on audit quality. The research reached a number of conclusions, most notably that the integration of the performance of internal and external auditors is a fundamental pillar for improving the quality of the audit process from a theoretical perspective, as it achieves coordination in planning, information exchange, and a reduction in duplication of audit efforts. The results of the descriptive analysis showed positive attitudes among the sample towards the importance of integration between internal and external auditing, especially with regard to its role in raising the efficiency of auditing procedures and enhancing the quality of financial reports.

title: Green supply chain management practices and firm performance through the direct and moderating roles of supply chain ecocentricity among manufacturing firms in Hawassa City, Ethiopia
summary: Growing environmental “pressures and increasing stakeholder expectations have intensified the need for firms to integrate sustainability into supply chain management. Although Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) practices are widely recognized as drivers of organizational performance, empirical evidence remains inconsistent, particularly in developing economies. Grounded in the Natural Resource-Based View and Stakeholder Theory, this study examines the effects of Green Supply Chain Management practices on firm performance while investigating the dual role of Supply Chain ecocentricity as both a direct determinant of firm performance and a moderating mechanism that influences the relationships between GSCM practices and firm performance. Survey data were collected from manufacturing firms in Hawassa City, Ethiopia, and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that green manufacturing and green distribution practices significantly improve firm performance, whereas green reverse logistics has a weaker but significant positive effect. In contrast, green procurement exhibits a significant negative association with firm performance. The findings further demonstrate that Supply Chain ecocentricity directly enhances firm performance and strengthens the performance effects of Green Supply Chain Management practices by reinforcing the effectiveness of environmentally oriented supply chain initiatives. These findings underscore the strategic importance of embedding ecological values within supply chain decision-making and extend the Natural Resource-Based View and Stakeholder Theory by demonstrating the dual role of Supply Chain ecocentricity as both a strategic organizational capability and a contextual mechanism that enhances the performance benefits of Green Supply Chain Management” practices in a developing-country context.

title: AI-Driven Self-Healing Supply Chains and the Future of Logistics Automation
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) enables self-healing capabilities in global supply chains and reshapes logistics automation. Employing a qualitative multi-case study design, data were collected through 42 semi-structured interviews across six multinational organisations in manufacturing, retail, and third-party logistics. Thematic analysis yielded four themes: AI-enabled disruption sensing; autonomous reconfiguration mechanisms; human-AI collaboration and workforce transformation; and ethical and governance considerations. Findings demonstrate that self-healing capability emerges from the dynamic interplay between AI infrastructure, adaptive organisational routines, and human agency - not from technology alone. Organisations embedding AI within a dynamic capabilities’ framework achieve measurable reductions in disruption recovery time and operational costs. A grounded theoretical model of AI-driven supply chain self-healing is proposed, integrating dynamic capabilities theory and complex adaptive systems theory. Practical implications for supply chain leaders and directions for future mixed-methods research are discussed.

title: Can Digital Transformation Promote Corporate Resilience Growth?
summary: In an increasingly uncertain business environment, digital transformation (DT) may help firms withstand external shocks and sustain long-term development. This study examines whether and how DT enhances corporate resilience (CR), conceptualized in terms of resistance ability and growth ability. Using panel data on Chinese listed firms from 2010 to 2022, DT is measured through annual-report text analysis. Firm- and year-fixed-effects regressions, instrumental-variable estimation, mediation analysis, and heterogeneity tests are employed to assess the effect of DT on CR and explore the underlying mechanisms. Empirical outcomes demonstrate that DT has excellent potential in empowering corporates to withstand external environment crises and gain long-term competitive advantage. This indicates that DT contributes to improving CR. Regarding transmission mechanisms, DT can improve the management innovation level with its powerful penetration and restructuring functions. This improvement in internal control capabilities significantly enhances CR. The heterogeneity outcomes demonstrate that the promotion impact of DT on CR is more particularly pronounced among non-high-tech companies, firms with high financing constraints, and enterprises operating in intense industry competition. These insights support governments in formulating digital-related policies and provide evidence for encouraging enterprises to enhance the application of digital technology and improve their resilience.

title: Revolutionizing hospital supply chain: machine learning for predictive risk assessment
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to identify and prioritize the risks associated with healthcare supply chain with a focus on hospital’s internal supply chain. Design/methodology/approach The study presents a machine learning model for hospital supply chain risk assessment. Through previous literature and interviews, 35 risk factors were identified, which were then used to devise a questionnaire aimed at assessing the probability and impact of these risk factors. A total of 140 responses were gathered from subject matter experts. Six machine learning algorithms, namely, Naïve Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) were used in this study. Techniques including holdout validation and k-fold cross-validation were used for evaluating the six classifiers. Findings Results from the feature subset selection process revealed that the most significant variables included “black market,” “delay in replacement of defective products,” “delay in delivery of imported products,” “defaulted suppliers,” “mismanagement of expired medicines,” “lack of planning,” “ban on import of raw materials” and “lack of budget.” While holdout validation results showed that Naïve Bayes achieved highest classification accuracy of 85.7%, the k-fold cross-validation indicated that RF, ANN and KNN outperformed NB, LR and SVM in terms of accuracy, highlighting their superior generalization capability. Originality/value The study fills an important research gap by providing valuable and novel insights for healthcare institutes and policymakers in making informed decisions regarding risk mitigation strategies, resource allocation and operational planning. By shifting their focus on the critical risk factors, stakeholders can prioritize their efforts and resources more effectively.

title: Unmasking greenwashing through the role of gender diversity and CSR committees in driving real sustainability in Chinese firms
summary: Greenwashing, the deliberate overstatement of a firm’s environmental performance, undermines stakeholder trust and threatens the credibility of corporate sustainability reporting. This study examines how three board attributes, gender diversity, independence, and directors’ international experience, influence greenwashing among Chinese listed firms, and whether Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) committees strengthen these governance effects. Drawing on 4,312 firm-year observations from 2016 to 2023, sourced from the CSMAR, Bloomberg, and Refinitiv (Asset4) databases, greenwashing is measured as the gap between a firm’s disclosed and actual ESG performance. The results indicate that board gender diversity, independence, and international experience are each associated with lower greenwashing, and that CSR committees strengthen these effects, reinforcing corporate accountability and disclosure quality. These findings offer empirical evidence that internal governance mechanisms, not only external regulation, shape firms’ environmental integrity, with implications for policymakers and corporate leaders seeking to improve the credibility of ESG reporting.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE CONSTRUCTION SECTOR IN ALBANIA AND THE CHALLENGES OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: The development of Albania’s construction sector has moved from entrepreneurial fragmentation toward larger projects, more formalized structures, and growing pressure to digitalize. Nevertheless, small enterprises continue to dominate its structure, and activity remains geographically concentrated. This article examines how these trends relate to the organizational requirements of digital transformation in a developing economy. The analysis draws on official statistics on enterprises, employment, planned investment and the sector’s contribution to GDP, together with a thematic review of international and regional literature on construction digitalization. The findings indicate that sectoral expansion does not necessarily entail growth in firm size, and that the composition of activity and fluctuations in demand affect opportunities for long-term investment in systems and skills. The article’s contribution is to connect evidence on Albania’s construction sector with three practical requirements of transformation: coordinating information among stakeholders, retaining knowledge from one project to the next, and integrating office and site operations. The Albanian case helps explain challenges faced by other construction markets characterized by small firms and developing institutional capacities, particularly in the Western Balkans.

title: SYSTEMIC APPROACH TO QUALITY MANAGEMENT IN THE CLIMATE ECONOMY, ENCOMPASSING CLIMATE FINANCE, ENVIRONMENTAL INNOVATION, AND GREEN EMPLOYMENT
summary: Quality management in the climate economy requires a systemic approach that integrates coordinated policy, institutional participation, and cross-sector collaboration among business, R&D, and investors.A systemic approach in this sphere involves targeted accumulation of climate finance in environmental innovations and green employment.The transition to the climate economy is based on a range of criteria and goals (parameters) for the quality management of sectoral development, which are informed by the country's sustainable development strategy.In this work, we identified leading approaches to the system management of quality in the climate economy, focusing on climate finance, environmental innovation, and green employment, thereby providing a theoretical and methodological framework for effective policy in this sphere.The research relies on the example of the EU, since this union has effective programmes and laws on the climate economy and implements them by attracting a wide range of participants.The research period is 2005-2024, due to historical prerequisites and the availability of relevant data.The analysis showed that the EU uses an effective systemic approach to managing the quality of products and services, which involves climate finance, environmental innovation, and green employment.However, there are certain problems with renewable energy and green employment.In the course of this research, we identified the main quality parameters, which are distinguished by the development of the climate economy: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, green energy use, circularity, resource efficiency, and continuous green energy supply.

title: A Quantitative Study on Digital Transformation and Fiscal Policy in Enhancing Financial Management and Investment Efficiency
summary: This study examines the interrelationships among Financial Management and Liquidity, Data Analytics and Financial Models, Investment and Portfolio, and Financing and Financial Markets in influencing Fiscal Policy and Economic Governance to strengthen financial stability and performance. Using a quantitative design with Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrapping analysis through SmartPLS version 3.0, the findings demonstrate that effective financial management and liquidity control significantly enhance capital efficiency and organizational profitability. The integration of data analytics and advanced financial models supported by artificial intelligence (AI) improves risk prediction and supports evidence-based financial decisions. Investment and portfolio diversification, particularly through sustainable and green investment practices, increase rationality in decision-making and promote environmentally responsible growth. Furthermore, financing innovations such as peer-to-peer (P2P) lending and research-based investment contribute to inclusive access to capital and transparency in financial markets. At the macro level, adaptive fiscal policies—through progressive taxation and regional revenue optimization—foster equitable development and economic resilience. Overall, the results confirm that the synergy between micro-level financial efficiency and macro-level fiscal governance is pivotal for creating a resilient, transparent, and sustainable financial system. The study provides theoretical insights and practical implications for policymakers and financial institutions in developing adaptive, digital-based financial models and sustainable fiscal governance aligned with long-term economic transformation.

title: Does gender influence ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies? Evidence from Asian economies
summary: Abstract ESG risks pose serious risks to the brand and viability of agri-food companies, making them more vulnerable than other industries that necessitates ESG reporting practices. However, this study evaluated the ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies, which were not the focus of previous research. The study investigates how ESG motivations and obstacles influence ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies in Asian countries. The study also evaluates the influence of gender as a moderator in ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies. To reach the objectives we used the quantitative method which comprised a quantitative investigation of 400 experts (100 from each country). The study used PLS-SEM to evaluate the influence of ESG motivations and obstacles in ESG reporting practices while PLS-MGA was used for examining the gender influence grounded in agency theory, stakeholder theory and legitimacy theory. The study revealed that ESG motivations and obstacles have a positive and significant influence on ESG reporting practices in agri-food companies. Motivations and challenges together account for 69.84% of the variation in ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies. ESG motivations have a high degree positive influence on ESG reporting practices compared to ESG obstacles. The study also revealed that as a moderator, gender has no significant influence in ESG reporting practices of agri-food companies. Legal structures provide a helpful basis for the development of ESG disclosure practices, and the level of ESG reporting in Asian agri-food companies is increasing gradually. For regulators, policymakers, and companies operating in developing countries, this study has important implications. Our work also has intriguing real-world applications for regulators, policymakers, and other players in the Asian market. The study suggests that authorities and policymakers should take proactive measures to strengthen the implementation of the ESG reporting assessment in order to enhance ESG reporting practices.
