title: Cost, Financing, and Institutional Barriers to Green Supply Chain Management Adoption in South-East Nigeria's Building Construction Sector
summary: The construction industry is essential to economic and social development through the provision of residential, commercial, institutional and infrastructure facilities. However, construction activities are associated with substantial consumption of natural resources, energy use, material extraction, transportation and waste generation. These environmental impacts extend across the construction supply chain, involving material manufacturers, suppliers, contractors, transport providers and other project stakeholders. The United Nations Environment Programme and Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction (2024) reported that buildings and construction account for approximately 32% of global energy consumption and 34% of global carbon dioxide emissions. These impacts have increased the need for approaches that integrate environmental considerations into construction processes and supply-chain activities.

title: Implementasi Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) oleh PT. Citra Palu Mineral (CPM): Studi Kasus dalam Pembuatan Produk Kantong Sampel di Kecamatan Mantikulore
summary: Program CSR di sektor pertambangan telah banyak diterapkan, akan tetapi, studi yang secara spesifik mengkaji pemberdayaan masyarakat lokal melalui keterlibatan langsung dalam rantai pasok alat penunjang operasional perusahaan masih sangat terbatas. Kebaruan penelitian ini terletak pada analisis model pemberdayaan ekonomi lokal berbasis integrasi rantai pasok produksi kantong sampel. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah menganalisis implementasi CSR pada PT. CPM dalam pembuatan produk kantong sampel dan mendeskripsikan dampak yang dihasilkan dari program CSR PT. CPM dalam pembuatan produk kantong sampel. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode penelitian kualitatif deskriptif dengan tipe studi kasus. Teknik pengumpulan data menggunakan observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menemukan bahwa; 1) implementasi CSR pada PT. CPM dalam pembuatan produk kantong sampel di Kecamatan Mantikulore terdiri atas beberapa tahapan, yaitu: koordinasi perusahaan dengan pihak terkait, pendaftaran terbuka, sosialisasi dan pelatihan, produksi, dan pengawasan serta evaluasi; dan 2) dampak program CSR PT. CPM dalam pembuatan produk kantong sampel terdiri atas dampak ekonomi, dampak peningkatan keterampilan, dan dampak sosial. Pada akhirnya, program pembuatan produk kantong sampel ini tidak hanya berfungsi untuk memenuhi kebutuhan operasional perusahaan, tetapi juga menjadi sarana pemberdayaan masyarakat di sekitar wilayah operasional perusahaan.

title: ITC Limited: a sustainable investment decision
summary: Learning outcomes Learning objectives are as follow: Case overview/synopsis The case examines whether a long-term, fundamentals-oriented fund should invest in the stock of ITC, a diversified Indian company with its largest business segment being cigarettes, after considering the relevant sustainability issues. The fund manager analysing ITC’s sustainability implications in June 2025 faces a dilemma in the presence of both favourable and unfavourable information and opinions concerning ITC’s sustainability. Being a tobacco products manufacturer, ITC is perceived as a “sin-stock”, while it is rated more favourably by the ESG rating agencies. While the company has an impressive track record of sustainability initiatives, does it adequately address the core issues? Should that matter to a fund catering to investors interested in financial returns? If sustainability is relevant to economic value, how should it be evaluated? The case illustrates the difference between impact and financial materiality. It also facilitates an understanding of how sustainability issues impact firm value and their implications for stock selection decisions in investment portfolio management. Lastly, it provides an opportunity to discuss the theoretical perspectives underlying a company’s sustainability-related activities, including the shareholder wealth maximisation objective, stakeholder concerns, and an organisation’s need for legitimacy. Complexity academic level Suitable for graduate or undergraduate level students in business management. Suitable courses include Sustainable Finance, Corporate Finance and Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management.

title: Blockchain-based pharmaceutical supply chain: a scalable and transparent model for drug traceability
summary: An efficient Supply Chain Management (SCM) system is crucial for ensuring product quality, safety, and reliability. The pharmaceutical supply chain includes all processes from the collection of raw materials to the secure delivery of drugs to end consumers. However, traditional pharmaceutical SCM systems often suffer from limited transparency, traceability, scalability, and security, which increase drug counterfeiting and trust issues among stakeholders. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Blockchain-Based Pharmaceutical Supply Chain (BBPSC) management system. The proposed scheme records, monitors, and verifies every stage of the pharmaceutical supply chain while ensuring data security. It integrates Filecoin for decentralized off-chain data storage, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA) for cryptographic authentication, and Ethereum-based smart contracts to enable secure, immutable, and automated supply chain operations. In the proposed system, the Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism is used to validate transactions before they are included in the blockchain, thereby enhancing efficiency and reducing computational overhead. Informal and formal security analyses presented in this paper demonstrate the resilience of the proposed scheme against major security attacks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed BBPSC scheme outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of throughput, communication cost, deployment cost, latency, and scalability.

title: AI in Supply Chain Analytics: Adaptive Decisioning via Fuzzy Behavioral Models
summary: The goal of this paper is to develop intelligent agents through fuzzy logic so that they can be capable of adaptability and context awareness in a simulated operational environment. Concentrating on dynamic interactions, fuzzy inference systems help agents to adjust their behavior according to proximity, velocity, and environmental conditions. The suggested approach helps to develop adaptive and robust automated decision-making systems. These components can optimize complex multi-stakeholder systems explicitly beneficial for modern supply chain systems. The paper states that AI can be used to enhance the flexibility and reactivity of logistics and inventory management systems, offering various technical and practical contributions.

title: Circularity beyond recycling: toward a regenerative supply chain philosophy a conceptual framework
summary: This conceptual paper on the shortcomings of the circular economy model and proposes an approach towards regenerative supply chains where there is an inherent philosophy of restoring the ecosystems in design, rather than addressing end-of-life recovery when recycling alone cannot reduce the environmental footprint. This conceptual framework is developed by conducting an iterative process of thematic analysis of the ecological economics, cradle-to-cradle approach, and complex adaptive system theories through the review of 39 peer-reviewed articles. This paper presents a conceptual and theoretical framework and not an empirical study. Existing circular economy concepts continue the practice of extraction and ignore the problems of rebound effects. The idea of regenerative supply chain is introduced to improve natural and socio-economic ecosystems using the combination of ecosystem services, digitization, and policymaking. Originality/Value: This paper offers a new concept of regenerative supply chain in which regeneration is viewed as a continuous, spiral process rather than optimization of closed-loop process, based on ecopoetic and relational biology approaches. The organizations would need to create new business models, measurement systems, and governing systems which would link economic incentives with ecological restoration. The model sees the supply chain as an agent for regeneration on a social level. As a conceptual framework, the propositions set out here need to be verified empirically across a range of industries and varied regional settings. No primary information was taken in, so every claim is only a theoretical proposal, plus an expected outcome, rather than a demonstrated result.

title: Incentivizing Sustainable Aviation Fuel: Supply Chain and Policy Insights from Brazil
summary: Abstract Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plays a central role in decarbonizing the aviation sector. Brazil is positioned to become a leader in SAF production and consumption from sugarcane-based ethanol. However, integrating SAF into the Brazilian sugarcane industry is challenging due to high production costs, an undeveloped SAF supply chain, and ethanol competition between ground and aviation transportation. The present study uses mixed-integer linear optimization to design SAF supply chains in Brazil under various blend requirements and design scenarios. Three sugarcane mills in São Paulo are identified for strategic SAF investments, with a recommended premium of 2.6 R$ L–1 (0.5 US$ L–1). Furthermore, SAF production increases net CO2 emissions by up to 2.7 Mt year–1 (relative to a 0% baseline) due to ethanol displacement. Sensitivity analysis reveals SAF conversion and emission targets for net-zero system emissions. These results provide several key insights to guide SAF supply chain growth, technology development, and policy design in Brazil. Finally, the general optimization framework provides a template for SAF capacity expansion worldwide.

title: Circuit Courts, Local Protectionism, and Upward Real Earnings Management: The Role of Judicial Reform
summary: Using China’s establishment of circuit courts as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines how judicial reform affects corporate behavior. Based on city-level and listed-firm data from 2012 to 2016, we find that circuit courts significantly suppress upward real earnings management in highly protectionist regions and mitigate protectionism-induced increases in firms’ relational expenditures and tax refunds. The effect is stronger where market competition is intense, legal institutions are weak, and internal governance is poor, revealing a substitution effect between judicial enforcement and market or governance mechanisms. These findings highlight circuit courts’ dual role in dismantling local protectionism and curbing corporate misconduct, underscoring the importance of rule-of-law institutions for market integration in emerging economies.

title: Investigating the Economic and Productivity Effects of Digital Transformation in Project Management
summary: Project management is being reshaped by artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, automation, data analytics, and digital project management platforms. Yet the expected economic and productivity gains are not always realized due to execution costs, skills gaps, integration challenges, and organizational resistance. This study analyses the effects of digital transformation on economic efficiency, productivity, workflow optimization, and project delivery, and examines the link between employee digital competency and transformation success. A mixed-methods design was used: a quantitative survey of 100 project employees and semi-structured interviews with 10 employees. Quantitative analysis employed frequencies, percentages, and descriptive statistics; qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Overall, perceptions of digital transformation were positive: 68%–78% agreed or strongly agreed that digital technologies improve cost efficiency, resource use, project performance, workflow efficiency, productivity, and delivery outcomes. Moreover, 74% associated higher employee digital competency with improved project results. Five themes emerged: economic efficiency and cost optimization; productivity and workflow optimization; employee digital competency; leadership and organizational culture; and data-driven decision-making and risk mitigation. Key hurdles remain: execution costs, resistance to change, skills gaps, and data quality. The study concludes that successful digital transformation depends on employee competence, effective leadership, organizational readiness, and disciplined execution conditions that can enhance project performance and economic value.

title: The Influence of Sales Growth and Earnings Management on Financial Performance: The Role of Firm Size Moderation
summary: This study analyzes the influence of sales growth and earnings management on financial performance and examines whether firm size moderates the relationship in Consumer Non-Cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the period 2021–2024. Financial performance is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), earnings management by discretionary accruals using the Modified Jones Model, sales growth by annual sales change, and firm size by the natural logarithm of total assets. The study uses a causal quantitative design with panel data and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) using EViews 12. Purposive sampling in the early stages resulted in 46 companies with 184 company-year observations; after outlier screening, 167 observations were used in the model estimation. The selected model was the Random Effects Model. The results showed that sales growth had no significant effect on financial performance (p = 0.2101), while earnings management had a positive and significant effect (p = 0.0126). Firm size significantly moderated the influence of sales growth on financial performance in a negative direction (p = 0.0488), thus acting as a pure moderator that weakened the sales growth–ROA relationship. Firm size was not proven to moderate the relationship between earnings management and financial performance (p = 0.4127). These findings suggest that revenue increases alone are not enough to increase profitability if operating costs and asset use are not managed efficiently, while reported ROA remains sensitive to discretionary accruals.

title: Green knowledge transaction networks, knowledge absorptive capacity and breakthrough green innovation
summary: Purpose Drawing on the knowledge-based view, structural holes theory and absorptive capacity theory, this study aims to examine how firms’ structural advantages in green knowledge transaction networks affect breakthrough green innovation. It further investigates the mechanisms through which knowledge retrieval ability, knowledge integration ability, and knowledge absorptive capacity shape this relationship. Design/methodology/approach This study measures the structural advantage of the green knowledge transaction network by the structural hole index and measures breakthrough green innovation by highly cited green invention patents within the same technology field. Findings The results show that structural advantages in green knowledge transaction networks are positively associated with breakthrough green innovation. This effect persists over time but gradually weakens. Mechanism tests indicate that knowledge retrieval ability and knowledge integration ability are important channels through which network structural advantages are transformed into breakthrough green innovation. The moderation results show that knowledge absorptive capacity strengthens the positive effect of green knowledge transaction network structural advantages on breakthrough green innovation. Further analysis shows that this effect is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises and firms in low-technology industries, while there is little difference in the effect between polluting and clean industries. Originality/value This study introduces green knowledge transaction networks into knowledge management research and incorporates knowledge retrieval ability, knowledge integration ability, and knowledge absorptive capacity into a unified analytical framework. It reveals the conversion logic through which green knowledge transaction networks affect breakthrough green innovation.

title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
summary: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. Drawing on fieldwork in two northern municipalities (São Miguel and Tarrafal) and 25 semi-structured interviews with community leaders and sand and gravel extractors, this article investigates why extraction persists despite a dense regulatory architecture. We find that extraction is a survivalist strategy primarily undertaken by women heads of household, for whom environmental regulation represents a direct threat to precarious livelihoods. Mobilising the "environmental state" framework and feminist political ecology (Nightingale, 2006). We argue that state intervention has tightened coastal enforcement but displaced extraction into riverbeds and hillsides, intensifying rather than reducing aggregate environmental pressure. We characterise this as "governing through precarity", an environmental state present in law and on highly visible beaches, though absent in inland sites where the poorest extractors work. By centring the politics of enforcement and social reproduction, the article contributes to global debates on artisanal extraction, gender, and informality in African Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

title: SLOW FOOD AND SUSTAINABLE LOCAL SUPPLY CHAINS IN PIEDMONT: BUILDING TRUST THROUGH SHORT NETWORKS
summary: Aim: This study explores consumer perceptions of slow food and sustainable local supply chains, using the event "Terra Madre -Salone del Gusto 2024" in Piedmont, Italy, as a case study.The objective was to identify motivational factors shaping consumer trust in short supply networks and to position the Piedmont configuration as a conceptual reference for future comparative research in Serbia and Southeast Europe, where traditional products strongly align with the principles of slow food.Material and methods: A structured questionnaire containing 32 Likert-scale items was distributed to 448 fair visitors.The measurement model, developed from the literature, was validated through exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis using SEM-AMOS.Reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity were assessed with CR, AVE, Fornell-Larcker, and HTMT criteria.Results: Four latent constructs were supported -Health Quality, Price Premium, Green Responsibility, and Local Trust -with strong psychometric properties.Structural paths among domains were small and not statistically significant (≈ -0.04 to +0.02), indicating parallel rather than sequential causal relations.Local Trust did not mediate the other domains.Conclusions: Findings suggest that support for short supply chains stems from coexisting, independent motivations.Managerial implications should therefore target each domain separately (quality and traceability cues, fair-price narratives, visible environmental practices, producer identity and transparency).The Piedmont configuration serves as a conceptual reference whose potential transferability to Serbia and Southeast Europe represents a promising avenue for future comparative research.

title: Digital transformation with female inclusion: opportunities, challenges and strategies to reduce technological gender gaps
summary: This study aims to synthesise the scientific evidence on digital transformation and female inclusion by identifying the institutional strategies, structural barriers, technological training initiatives, and equity outcomes that shape women's participation in digital transformation processes. To achieve this objective, a systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, integrating empirical and theoretical evidence to analyse the relationships among institutional policies, digital transformation, gender equity, and women's inclusion across diverse socioeconomic and organisational contexts. The findings reveal that digital transformation is not determined exclusively by technological advancement but is shaped by a complex interaction of institutional, social, and cultural factors. In this regard, the review identifies persistent barriers associated with digital skills gaps, governance limitations, infrastructure inequalities, and broader gender disparities that continue to restrict women's participation in digital ecosystems. However, the evidence also highlights the relevance of coordinated public policies, organisational strategies, and digital training initiatives as mechanisms to strengthen women's capabilities and promote more inclusive transformation processes. By consolidating fragmented evidence from multiple contexts, this study provides an integrated perspective on the relationship between digital transformation and female inclusion. The proposed analytical framework contributes to a deeper understanding of how institutional policies, structural conditions, and digital capabilities interact to foster equitable and sustainable digital transformation, offering insights for researchers, policymakers, and organisations seeking to advance gender-responsive digital development.

title: Evolutionary game analysis of cooperative technology upgrading in EV battery reverse supply chains
summary: Achieving efficient recycling of end-of-life electric vehicle (EV) batteries requires both technology and strategic coordination among stakeholders. This study examines cooperative technological upgrading in EV battery recycling using evolutionary game theory. A bilateral model is developed to analyze strategic interactions between manufacturers and recyclers, and then extended to a tripartite framework by introducing government intervention. Numerical simulations and sensitivity analyses yield three main findings. First, initial strategy probabilities affect convergence speed but not long-run equilibria. Second, stable cooperation emerges only when the benefits of improved recyclability and recovery efficiency exceed upgrading costs. Third, government subsidies increase the willingness of firms to adopt technology upgrading strategies, while interfirm penalty and compensation mechanisms discourage passive and unilateral behavior. Higher cooperative benefits further reduce the dependence of firms on government support, thereby jointly improving incentive compatibility and system stability. The findings contribute to understanding cooperation mechanisms in battery reverse supply chains and provide insights for the design of effective recycling policies.

title: Supply chain readiness and export performance in Africa: evidence from interpretable machine learning
summary: Purpose This study examines whether a multidimensional supply-chain readiness system predicts export performance across African economies and whether the relationships persist when export performance is measured through aggregate value, extensive product breadth and intensive product depth rather than exports relative to GDP. Design/methodology/approach The analysis begins with a 54-country, 1985–2024 country-year grid while retaining original missing observations. Export intensity is retained as a benchmark. Additional outcomes comprise log merchandise export value, the number of exported HS-6 products and log export value per HS-6 product. Ridge, Random Forest, Extra Trees and Gradient Boosting are assessed with temporal, random, country-group and rolling validation. Findings Extra Trees remains the strongest benchmark model (R-squared = 0.651). Predictive performance is also high for log merchandise exports (R-squared = 0.926), exported HS-6 product breadth (R-squared = 0.891) and log exports per HS-6 product (R-squared = 0.824). The complete-case benchmark, estimated without numerical imputation, records R-squared = 0.737. Country demeaning lowers R-squared to 0.242 for export intensity and 0.283 for log merchandise exports, confirming that pooled machine learning captures substantial between-country structure. Within-country importance nevertheless retains industry employment for export intensity and manufacturing value added for merchandise export value as leading readiness signals. Originality/value The study combines interpretable machine learning with alternative export-performance margins, explicit missing-data sensitivity and a pooled-versus-within-country bridge. The results distinguish predictive cross-country structure from within-country change and provide a more cautious basis for connecting supply-chain readiness to export breadth and depth.

title: Digital Social Administration: A New Paradigm for Understanding the Digital Transformation of Welfare
summary: ABSTRACT Digital public administration scholarship has expanded on broad trends in government digitalization, yet its generic categories, such as ‘citizen’, ‘user’ and ‘service’, systematically overlook what is distinctive about welfare administration. From automated debt recovery and predictive risk modelling to algorithmic child protection and emerging generative AI applications, the digital transformation of social policy creates profound dilemmas that generic frameworks cannot address. This paper proposes digital social administration (DSA) as a new conceptual paradigm—the ensemble of digitized and automated systems, data infrastructures, algorithmic tools and organizational practices through which welfare states assess eligibility, allocate benefits, govern risk and manage disadvantaged populations. We develop the TOV Three‐Dimensional Analytical Framework to operationalize this paradigm, focusing on the Technical, Organizational and Valuational dimensions of DSA and their relationships. Applying the framework to four signature dilemmas, and considering the emerging challenges posed by advanced AI and AGI demonstrates its ability to reveal dynamics that single‐dimensional approaches overlook. DSA constitutes a qualitatively new administrative form, comparable to the bureau‐professional state or new public management, and demands concepts adequate to its specificity. We conclude by outlining a research agenda organized around the TOV dimensions and identifying implications for social policy, practice, advocacy and legal reform.

title: Digital Transformation and Eco‐Innovation: Evidence on the Twin Transition of European Companies
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how the adoption of digital technologies drives corporate eco‐innovation among companies listed in the European Union and the United Kingdom, where firms' twin transition, digital and green, is essential to achieving ambitious sustainability goals. Using performance‐based measures of eco‐innovation and regression analyses, we investigate the effects of both overall corporate digital transformation and the adoption of specific digital technologies. Our results show that corporate digitalization enhances eco‐innovation, with a more pronounced effect on eco‐product innovation. We also find that sustainability performance plays an important mediating role, channeling the effects of digitalization toward eco‐innovation. As digital transformation increasingly impacts all areas of corporate activity, including how firms identify and respond to sustainability challenges, its contribution to eco‐innovation extends beyond direct technological effects, as by improving sustainability performance, digitalization creates conditions that foster eco‐innovation. These findings highlight how digitalization can reinforce the green transition, promote eco‐innovation, and ultimately support sustainable growth.

title: Internal Control and Sustainable Corporate Responsibility: Evidence from China
summary: This study uses data from Chinese A-share listed firms between 2008 and 2022 and finds that higher internal control quality (ICQ) is significantly associated with better corporate social responsibility (CSR). The result is robust to alternative measures, instrumental variables, lagged ICQ, propensity-score matching, multi-period difference-in-differences, and uninterpolated data. Evidence supports four mechanisms: lower agency costs, enhanced reputation, stronger responsibility-oriented culture, and more efficient resource allocation. The relationship is stronger in non-high-tech, labor-intensive, and indirect-to-consumer industries, weakened by business complexity, and strengthened by analyst attention. These findings extend internal control beyond financial reporting and compliance to responsible and sustainable corporate conduct.

title: The impact of digital transformation and operational management on the financial performance of MSMEs in India
summary: The study investigates the impact of operational management and digital technology transformation on the financial performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in western India. This research examines the combined impact of these factors on the financial and operational outcomes of MSMEs, offering insights for business owners and policymakers. The study is based on empirical analysis of responses from 140 business owners and managers of MSMEs across industrial clusters in western India, using structured Likert scale questionnaires to assess relationships between operational management, technology transformation, and financial performance through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) analysis. Findings indicate that both constructs positively influence financial performance, with technology transformation showing a comparatively stronger effect. Businesses leveraging both effective operational strategies and digital tools experience higher profitability, return on assets, and return on investment. The study further reveals significant differences in operational and technological capabilities across firm size categories, with medium-sized enterprises outperforming micro and small enterprises. The geographical scope is limited to select industrial clusters in western India, and findings may not be generalizable across India given regional variation. The study emphasizes that MSMEs must integrate operational excellence with digital innovation to remain competitive in an evolving market.

title: Managing global supply chains during a crisis: exploring the drivers of relational agility and relationship identity
summary: This research investigates how global supply chain partners’ perceptions and behaviours evolved during the COVID-19 pandemic and how these shifts shaped relational agility and relationship identity. Adopting an abductive, exploratory design, the study draws on in-depth interviews with managers from 18 internationally connected firms. The findings identify relational agility as a dynamic inter-organisational capability comprising enhanced communication, heightened awareness of partner changes, and increased adaptability. These dimensions create the relational conditions through which firms engage in five identity work approaches: discursive, dramaturgical, symbolic, psychodynamic, and socio-cognitive, contributing to relationship identity development during crises. By integrating relational agility with identity work, the study demonstrates how adaptive relational practices enable identity work and relationship identity development during disruption. The research contributes by advancing relational agility as a distinct capability, extending identity work theory to inter-organisational supply chain contexts, and explaining how relational agility and identity work shape supply chain relationships during crises.

title: Advancing sustainability in food and drink supply chains through additive manufacturing: A systematic literature review
summary: This systematic literature review (SLR) explores the transformative role of additive manufacturing, commonly known as 3D printing, in fostering sustainable supply chains for food. Utilizing the Antecedent, Decision, and Outcome (ADO) framework, this study synthesizes insights from 66 scholarly works to examine how additive manufacturing addresses inefficiencies, waste, and demand variability in food supply chains. Five key additive manufacturing-enabled supply chain strategies—Distributed Localized Manufacturing (DLM), in-house production, delayed production, mass customization, and on-demand production—are critically analysed for their sustainability impact across economic, environmental, and social dimensions. The findings highlight additive manufacturing’s potential to reduce waste, enhance production agility, lower transportation emissions, and enable personalized nutrition. However, barriers such as high material costs, regulatory challenges, and technological limitations remain significant hurdles to widespread adoption. This study contributes to the discourse on sustainable supply chain transformation by proposing a conceptual framework that aligns additive manufacturing strategies with sustainability objectives. The insights provided serve as a valuable resource for industry stakeholders and policymakers seeking to leverage additive manufacturing for a more resilient and sustainable food supply chain.

title: A Digital Transformation Framework for AI-Enabled Electric Vehicle Charging in Smart Cities
summary: As cities move towards electrification and sustainability through the increased use of electric vehicles (EV), these new modes of mobility will continue to change urban transportation. However, deploying the required EV charged infrastructure at scale across large urban centers will introduce operational, technology and energy management complexities. This study offers a comprehensive digital transformation framework for AI-based EV charging systems that increase grid reliability, support user convenience and improve energy efficiency. This comprehensive framework facilitates the integration of AI and IoT connectivity via cloud-based platforms and smart grid technologies, thus creating an intelligent and adaptive system. The research has explored problems associated with dynamic load balancing, integrating renewable energy, predictive maintenance, and estimating demand in real-time. This study used a data-driven approach to optimize the EVs, charging stations, utilities, and city infrastructures with seamless communication through digital technologies. Additionally, further, this study examined the importance of utilizing digital platforms to build scalable infrastructure, increase cyber resilience, and create a user-centric service delivery model. Using simulation-based testing, the study has shown improved EV charging efficiencies and reductions in peak electrical loads and operational costs. This model allows policymakers, city planners, and energy providers to develop resilient, sustainable, and intelligent EV charging systems. Furthermore, this framework reaffirms a larger global vision of carbon-neutral smart cities powered by digitally enabled mobility ecosystems.

title: High-value-added forest product exports, the digital economy, and the efficiency of forest ecological product value realization
summary: As ecological product value realization advances and green trade rules evolve, the relationship between high-value-added forest product exports and forest ecological product value realization efficiency has become increasingly important. Using a balanced panel dataset covering 31 Chinese provinces from 2015 to 2023, this study measures forest ecological-product value realization efficiency and employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the effects of high-value-added forest product exports and the digital economy. We further assess forestry industrial upgrading as a potential transmission channel and examine the moderating and threshold roles of the digital economy. The results show that both high-value-added forest product exports and digital economy development were both significantly and positively associated with the value-realization efficiency of forest ecological products, and the results remained consistent across multiple robustness checks. Channel testing showed that high-value-added forest product exports were significantly and positively associated with forestry industrial upgrading at the 5% level, supporting the industrial-structure channel. Interaction-term and threshold tests showed that higher levels of digital economy development strengthened the positive association between high-value-added forest product exports and the value-realization efficiency of forest ecological products; this association strengthened further when the digital economy index exceeded 0.2833 (approximately the 78.5th percentile of the sample). Heterogeneity analysis showed that the foregoing positive association was more pronounced in eastern regions, regions with stronger environmental regulation, and regions with greater forest-resource endowments; the positive association between digital economy development and the value-realization efficiency of forest ecological products was stronger in central and western regions and in regions with lower forest cover. The findings provide empirical evidence for promoting high-value-added forest product exports, harnessing the enabling role of digital trade, and efficiently realizing the value of forest ecological products.

title: Extrapolating CSR–HRM interdependencies and employee well-being for sustainable workplaces in generative AI era
summary: The development of generative AI (GAI) capabilities has led corporate entities to rethink their strategic initiatives towards sustainable workforce management. This dynamism has been broadly identified as a concern for managerial teams. Despite strong consensus on the roles of organizational human resources and corporate governance in managing the deployment of GAI mechanisms, specific factors contributing to each orientation remain unidentified. The current study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive review of factors that may affect sustainability orientation and employee well-being in the context of GAI implementation. The study utilized total interpretive structural modeling (TISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to the classification (MICMAC) method to develop the hierarchical relationship model. The study identified 16 factors: nine attributed to human resource management (HRM) and seven to the corporate social responsibility (CSR) domain. The study develops an expert-informed structural representation of the interrelationships between the two categories of designated factors. The outcomes identify two foundational factors as independent drivers and one dependent factor related to the social assessment of technology from a CSR perspective. The findings provide a structured interpretation of the interdependence between HRM and CSR factors and their implications for sustainable workforce management and employee health in SMEs. The study offers novel managerial implications on the relative orientations of driving and dependency factors for managing a sustainable workforce while supporting new technology development in the SME context.

title: Food fraud in Nigeria: A qualitative study of food supply chain actors, healthcare professionals, and regulatory officials
summary: Food fraud is an emerging concern in Nigeria with implications for food security, public health, and economic stability. This qualitative study aims to investigate the perspectives from three key stakeholder groups: food supply chain actors, healthcare professionals, and regulatory officials on drivers of food fraud, barriers to effective control, and strategies for prevention. Face-to-face or online semi-structured interviews were conducted with 36 participants ranging from stakeholders working in the food supply chain (n = 13), healthcare professionals (n = 9); and regulatory officials including National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), Nigerian Customs Service and Consumers Protection Council (n = 14). Interviews were conducted between June 2023 and January 2024. Qualitative data were analysed using thematic analysis. Five interrelated themes were identified: (i) food fraud as deliberate deception in the food system; (ii) structural and economic drivers of food fraud; (iii) food fraud as a public health and socio-economic threat; (iv) weak institutional capacity undermining food fraud control; and (v) coordinated strategies for prevention. Key drivers included inflation, high raw material and production costs, economic hardship, and financial gain. Across all stakeholder groups, weak institutional capacity was identified as a major barrier to effective control, including shortages of regulatory staff, equipment, funding, vehicles, and security concerns. Participants also highlighted corruption as a factor that may further weaken enforcement. This is the first study exploring in-depth perceptions of food fraud, drivers, barriers for effective control and mitigating strategies among three key stakeholders including those involved in food supply chain, healthcare and regulatory control in Nigeria.

title: The impact of supply chain complexity and incongruence on operational resilience: the mediating role of adaptive learning and resource specificity
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how firms sustain operational resilience under high supply chain (SC) complexity and incongruence in operational complexity across partners, and to test whether adaptive learning and resource specificity mediate these effects. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in complex adaptive systems theory, we investigate the mediating roles of adaptive learning and resource specificity in fostering resilience under conditions of high SC complexity and incongruence. Incongruence refers to the misalignment in operational complexity that a focal firm experiences across key SC partners (e.g. suppliers and third-party logistics providers) when fulfilling the same client orders. We analyse firm-level data from European companies and apply latent congruence modelling to test the hypotheses. Findings Both adaptive learning and resource specificity mediate the relationship between SC complexity level and resilience, underscoring their essential roles in managing complexity. When faced with SC incongruence, firms sustain resilience by intensifying adaptive learning in relationships involving lower-complexity operations, aligning them with more demanding ones elsewhere in the chain. Originality/value This study empirically demonstrates how firms cultivate resilience within complex operational environments through adaptive mechanisms. It advances theory by uncovering the role of SC incongruence, a critical yet underexplored structural condition in shaping firms' adaptive learning to sustain resilience. In practice, the findings offer guidance for firms navigating heterogeneous, high-complexity supply networks, highlighting adaptive mechanisms as strategic levers for building resilient operations.

title: Rare Earth Elements in Chile: A Critical Review of Primary, Secondary and Marine Resources, Metallurgical Recoverability and Future Supply Chain Opportunities
summary: The economic value of rare earth elements (REE) is concentrated in Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb. The supply chain for these elements is dominated by a single country, China, which accounts for about 60% of mined production, over 90% of refinement, and nearly 95% of permanent magnet manufacturing. This shifts the critical question from geological availability to the capacity to convert resources into products. Chile hosts several domain types for REE: ion-adsorption regoliths, primary mineralization associated with skarn, iron oxide–apatite (IOA) and iron oxide copper–gold (IOCG) systems, pegmatites and placers, and an Exclusive Economic Zone with marine occurrences. The inventory is organized using a five-level evidence scale, compiled through structured searches of indexed databases and institutional repositories under explicit inclusion criteria. Only one record reaches level 1, Penco, with 27.5 Mt Measured and Indicated at 2292 ppm TREO and 62.9 kt contained TREO. Its grade is two to three times higher than that of ion-adsorption deposits abroad, but its tonnage is one to two orders of magnitude lower. Recoveries vary by element, from 19.53% for Nd to 43.23% for Dy, meaning that the REE oxide it contains does not equate to fully recoverable product. Nahuelbuta reaches 2000 ppm exchangeable, Cerro Carmen contributes 19.81 Mt containing 8203 t of rare earth materials and 1811 t of U, and El Buitre contains 6.6 Mt at 337 mg/kg. Reported concentrations span four orders of magnitude, but only two of the five measurement scales include an associated tonnage. Metallurgical recoverability follows the same pattern: saline desorption is mature and retains Th and U in the solid residue, acid leaching of copper residues reaches 64.5% at laboratory scale, the monazite–xenotime and apatite routes are proven but untested on Chilean material, and no domain has demonstrated separation capability. Opportunities lie in by-product recovery from iron and copper operations, modular development of the central-southern corridor, and domestic separation. Converting the available evidence into comparable figures would reshape the national hierarchy more than additional exploration.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AND PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCY DEVELOPMENT IN THE ACCOUNTING PROFESSION: EVIDENCE FROM AN EMERGING ECONOMY
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the accounting profession by enhancing financial reporting, data analysis, and decision-making. However, empirical evidence on its influence on the professional competency development of accountants in emerging economies remains limited. This study examined the influence of AI on the professional competency development of professional accountants in South West Nigeria. A descriptive survey design was adopted, involving 312 professional accountants selected from accounting firms using a snowball sampling technique. Data were collected through a validated structured questionnaire (AI-PAS-Q) with a reliability coefficient of Cronbach's α = 0.84. Descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) answered the research questions, while an independent samples t-test tested the hypothesis at the 0.05 significance level. The findings revealed that AI adoption was limited (Grand Mean = 2.30), mainly due to inadequate digital infrastructure, weak organizational governance, and skills shortages. AI was primarily applied to financial reporting and invoice automation. Despite the low adoption level, AI positively influenced professional competency development (Grand Mean = 2.56), particularly in data analysis, financial reporting, and digital competence, while lower competency gains were recorded in professional judgement, fraud detection, advisory services, and client communication. A statistically significant gender difference in AI skill acquisition was found (t = 2.19, df = 310, p = .029). The study concludes that AI can strengthen accountants' competencies when supported by adequate infrastructure, continuous professional development, and effective regulatory frameworks, and recommends greater institutional investment in AI capacity building and governance

title: When does the pay gap pay off? Vertical and horizontal TMT pay dispersion and corporate governance in US hotels
summary: Purpose This study examines the distinct effects of vertical and horizontal top management team (TMT) pay dispersion on hotel firm performance, integrating tournament, expectancy, social comparison and equity theories, and investigates the moderating roles of key corporate governance mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from US publicly traded hotel firms, this study employs a two-way fixed effects model integrated with the Gaussian Copula approach (GCM_FE) to estimate the direct effects of pay dispersion and the moderating roles of corporate governance mechanisms, including board size, board independence, insider equity ownership and CEO duality. Findings After correcting for the endogeneity of pay dispersion, vertical pay dispersion has no significant association with firm performance. Instead, its effect is governance-contingent, strengthened by board independence and weakened by concentrated insider ownership and CEO duality. Horizontal pay dispersion shows no significant direct or moderated effect, indicating that the performance consequences of TMT pay dispersion are governance-dependent rather than uniform. Practical implications Hotel boards should condition vertical pay differentiation on verifiable governance safeguards rather than assuming wider gaps are uniformly motivating, and investors and analysts should interpret disclosed pay gaps in light of a firm's governance structure rather than treating them as uniformly informative. Originality/value This paper advances the strategic management and corporate governance literature by isolating the divergent mechanisms of vertical and horizontal pay dispersion, and by delineating specific corporate governance configurations as boundary conditions that either optimize or undermine the motivational efficacy of executive compensation.

title: Ownership structure and firm performance in G5 countries: a dynamic panel ARDL approach with a focus on employee shareholding
summary: Purpose This study examines how institutional, concentrated and employee ownership structures impact the financial performance of publicly listed firms across G5 countries. It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how different ownership types influence firm performance metrics (ROA and Tobin's Q) while addressing gaps in existing literature regar, Faculty of Economic Sciences and Management of Tunis ding comparative cross-country analysis and the underexplored role of employee ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research utilizes panel data from 550 firms across G5 nations spanning 2016–2023. The methodology centers on the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model using the pooled mean group (PMG) estimator, which accommodates mixed-order integration of variables and enables simultaneous examination of short-run adjustments and long-run relationships. Robustness checks include panel unit root tests and cointegration analysis. Findings The analysis reveals that employee shareholding has a significant positive long-run relationship with firm profitability, though no short-term effect. For institutional ownership no significant impact on profitability was found in either the long or short run. Conversely, majority shareholder ownership demonstrates a significant positive long-term association with firm profitability but an insignificant short-term effect. Practical implications The findings offer useful implications for corporate governance. The positive effect of ownership concentration suggests that large shareholders can enhance monitoring and reduce agency conflicts, thereby improving firm performance. In contrast, the insignificant impact of institutional ownership indicates limited monitoring by institutional investors. This highlights the need to encourage more active institutional investor participation in corporate governance. Originality/value This research represents the first comprehensive application of ARDL panel techniques to simultaneously analyze all three ownership types across major economies. It systematically incorporates employee ownership into performance analysis, an aspect frequently overlooked in financial research. The comparative framework across G5 countries reveals how institutional contexts moderate ownership-performance relationships, particularly showing stronger employee ownership effects in coordinated market economies.

title: Methodological Evaluation and Reliability Forecasting for District Hospital Systems in Ethiopia: A Time-Series Meta-Analysis
summary: District hospitals are critical nodes in healthcare delivery, yet systematic evaluations of their operational reliability in low-resource settings are scarce. Existing assessments often lack robust, predictive methodologies to inform proactive system strengthening. This meta-analysis aims to methodologically evaluate published and grey literature on district hospital systems in Ethiopia and to develop a time-series forecasting model for predicting system reliability. We conducted a systematic search for time-series and longitudinal studies reporting on hospital operational metrics. A bespoke Bayesian structural time-series model was fitted to synthesise data, forecasting reliability as a function of infrastructural, staffing, and supply chain covariates. The core forecasting equation is $R_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{t-1} + \phi R_{t-1} + \epsilon_t$, where $R_t$ is reliability. Model uncertainty was quantified using 95% credible intervals. The methodological review identified a predominant focus on static snapshots rather than dynamic analysis. The forecasting model indicates a strong positive association between supply chain continuity and predicted reliability, with a one-standard-deviation improvement in supply metrics increasing forecasted reliability by 15.2 percentage points (95% CrI: 11.8 to 18.6). The analysis demonstrates the feasibility and utility of applying time-series meta-analytic forecasting to hospital system evaluation, revealing key dynamic drivers of reliability often obscured in cross-sectional studies. Future research and monitoring should adopt longitudinal designs to capture system dynamics. Health planners should integrate predictive reliability modelling, particularly focusing on supply chain resilience, into routine hospital management. health systems research, operational research, predictive modelling, Bayesian analysis, healthcare forecasting, resource-limited settings This study provides a novel methodological framework for the predictive meta-analysis of health system reliability, generating a validated forecasting tool specific to the district hospital context.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR SERVICE QUALITY
summary: The tourism and hospitality sector is experiencing a rapid digital transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, mobile technologies, automation, and increasingly connected service environments. These technologies are changing how travellers search for information, select accommodation, communicate with service providers, and evaluate their experiences. At the same time, hotels and tourism enterprises are using digital tools to improve operational efficiency, personalise services, support employees, and make decisions based on data. This article examines the main opportunities and challenges associated with AI and digital transformation in tourism and hospitality, with particular attention to service quality and the role of human employees. The paper uses a narrative review of recent international research and policy literature. The analysis indicates that AI can support customer communication, demand forecasting, recommendation systems, revenue management, multilingual assistance, and routine operational tasks. However, successful digital transformation depends not only on technology but also on employee skills, data governance, privacy protection, service design, and the preservation of meaningful human interaction. The article argues that technology should be implemented as a tool for strengthening hospitality rather than as a substitute for hospitality itself. The findings are relevant to hospitality managers, tourism educators, students, and policymakers seeking to prepare the sector for a more digital and data-informed future.

title: Digital Transformation of Pharmaceutical Production Planning in Saudi Arabia Using Integrated ERP Systems
summary: Saudi Arabia is pursuing pharmaceutical localization, industrial diversification, health security, and digital transformation under Vision 2030. Yet local manufacturing capacity alone does not guarantee reliable medicine supply. Pharmaceutical plants must convert volatile demand, imported-material constraints, validated process capacity, quality-release requirements, and regulatory obligations into executable production plans. Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems can provide the digital backbone for this task, but value depends on integration with manufacturing execution, quality, laboratory, warehouse, maintenance, supplier, and advanced planning systems. This integrative review examines how ERP-enabled digital transformation can strengthen pharmaceutical production planning in Saudi Arabia. Recent pharmaceutical and Industry 4.0 literature is synthesized with Saudi policy and regulatory sources to identify planning capabilities, integration requirements, governance risks, and implementation priorities. The review argues that ERP should be treated not as an administrative transaction platform but as the controlled planning layer connecting demand, master production scheduling, material requirements planning, finite capacity, procurement, inventory, manufacturing execution, and batch release. A six-domain framework is proposed covering master-data integrity, integrated planning, execution visibility, quality-by-design information flows, analytics, and governance. The paper also presents an architecture for ERP-MES-QMS-LIMS-WMS-APS integration, a balanced KPI framework, and a phased 2026–2030 roadmap. For Saudi pharmaceutical manufacturers, the expected strategic value is improved schedule reliability, material readiness, capacity utilization, traceability, technology-transfer readiness, and resilience. The central conclusion is that digital transformation of planning should be built around validated processes, standardized data, cross-functional governance, and progressive integration rather than isolated technology deployment.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR SERVICE QUALITY
summary: The tourism and hospitality sector is experiencing a rapid digital transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, mobile technologies, automation, and increasingly connected service environments. These technologies are changing how travellers search for information, select accommodation, communicate with service providers, and evaluate their experiences. At the same time, hotels and tourism enterprises are using digital tools to improve operational efficiency, personalise services, support employees, and make decisions based on data. This article examines the main opportunities and challenges associated with AI and digital transformation in tourism and hospitality, with particular attention to service quality and the role of human employees. The paper uses a narrative review of recent international research and policy literature. The analysis indicates that AI can support customer communication, demand forecasting, recommendation systems, revenue management, multilingual assistance, and routine operational tasks. However, successful digital transformation depends not only on technology but also on employee skills, data governance, privacy protection, service design, and the preservation of meaningful human interaction. The article argues that technology should be implemented as a tool for strengthening hospitality rather than as a substitute for hospitality itself. The findings are relevant to hospitality managers, tourism educators, students, and policymakers seeking to prepare the sector for a more digital and data-informed future.

title: Digital Transformation of Firms and the Quality of Forward-Looking Disclosures: Through the Lens of Dynamic Capabilities
summary: Grounded in the dynamic capabilities theory, this paper investigates the economic consequences of corporate digital transformation on annual report linguistic tone and the quality of forward-looking information disclosure. Leveraging a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we adopt textual analysis, multi-dimensional textual indicators, staggered DID, PSM and a series of identification strategies to alleviate potential endogeneity concerns and conduct comprehensive robustness tests. We find robust evidence that digital transformation significantly improves the quality of forward-looking disclosures by optimizing hierarchical forward-looking disclosure performance, including authentic managerial optimistic expectations and standardized tone management behavior. These findings withstand endogeneity tests and alternative robustness checks. Furthermore, our cross-sectional analyses indicate that the positive impact is more pronounced for firms receiving substantial government subsidies or pursuing a cost leadership strategy, but is attenuated by high levels of R&D investment. Our research clarifies how digital transformation reshapes multi-layered forward-looking disclosure practices under the dynamic capabilities framework.

title: TAM-ECM Integration in Digital Transformation and Port Employee Performance: A Bibliometric Systematic Review
summary: Digital transformation in port operations requires rapid technology adoption, yet its effects from initial acceptance to continued use and employee performance remain theoretically fragmented. This study aims to identify research trends, map intellectual structures and thematic clusters, and identify research gaps to develop an integrative Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)-Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM) framework linking digital transformation, technology acceptance, continuous use, and employee performance in the port, maritime, and logistics sectors. This Bibliometric and Systematic Literature Review (B-SLR) integrates TAM and ECM in maritime logistics using Scopus data, with a Macro Pool (n = 451) analyzed via VOSviewer and a Micro Pool (n = 35) synthesized via RStudio. Bibliometric co-occurrence and coupling analyses identify key thematic clusters bridging initial adoption and long-term work routine stabilization. The qualitative synthesis reveals that digital transformation does not automatically translate into performance gains; instead, it is heavily mediated by individual cognitive and behavioral variables. The main findings show that TAM serves as an initial cognitive gateway shaping perceived usefulness and ease of use, while ECM acts as a continuance bridge driven by expectation confirmation and user satisfaction. This review addresses remaining theoretical gaps by proposing a sequential TAM-ECM conceptual framework specifically designed to evaluate port employee performance.

title: Litmus: Evaluating the Resilience of Blockchain-Enabled Software Systems for Supply Chains via Architecture Modeling and Chaos Injection
summary: Resilience is vital to blockchain-enabled software systems for supply chains (ChainFusion) and enables them to automatically adapt and continue providing their service when adverse situations occur. Since the notion of resilience in ChainFusion encompasses both the characteristics of a blockchain-enabled software system and the features of supply chains, complex trade-offs often exist among its resilience metrics. Furthermore, while blockchain technology provides novel mechanisms for enhancing resilience, it also inevitably introduces new resilience-related challenges. Therefore, when evaluating the resilience, it is crucial to evaluate the impact of blockchain technology on its resilience. In this paper, we propose Litmus, a method for evaluating the resilience of Chain-Fusion via architecture modeling and chaos injection. Litmus first models the system architecture using activity diagrams and extracts the minimal paths of the business process. Litmus then evaluates the resilience and outputs resilience issues by continuously injecting chaos into the system and monitoring variations in system state resilience curve. We assess the quality of Litmus by comparison with related work and through ablation experiments. We conduct case studies on a shipbuilding supply chain to evaluate the effectiveness of Litmus. Litmus identifies three previously unknown potential resilience issues. Furthermore, the studies indicate that blockchain behaviors, resilience mapping relationships, disturbance propagation paths, and disturbance types and intensities all impact the resilience of ChainFusion.

title: The Prudent Risk-Taking Equilibrium
summary: Objective: We examine how the effectiveness of pay-for-performance (PFP) systems in aligning managerial behavior with shareholder value depends on the joint interaction between executive risk appetite and corporate governance quality. We propose a “Prudent Risk-Taking Equilibrium” to explain how these opposing forces interact and influence incentive-system outcomes. Method: The sample comprises 1,106 firm-year observations from companies listed on the B3 (2018–2024), following the mandatory implementation of the Brazilian Corporate Governance Code. We employed multivariate panel-data regression models with firm and year fixed effects to test a three-way interaction among PFP structures, executive risk appetite, and governance compliance. Results: The findings indicate that high executive risk appetite strengthens the effects of short-term PFP but diminishes the outcomes of long-term PFP, whereas corporate governance has the opposite effect. The significant three-way interaction shows that strong governance channels high risk appetite toward effective performance. Governance substitutes for short-term bonuses and complements long-term incentives, ensuring that aggressive risk-taking generates sustainable value. Contributions: This research advances Agency Theory and the Behavioral Agency Model by demonstrating that governance mechanisms serve as channels that influence executive behavior. The empirical evidence confirms the effectiveness of the Brazilian Corporate Governance Code’s “comply-or-explain” approach, indicating that adherence to governance best practices yields tangible economic benefits by improving incentive effectiveness. In practical terms, the findings emphasize that compensation schemes should be tailored to the firm’s governance maturity and executive characteristics.

title: Configuration Paths of AI-Driven Urban Green Innovation: A Dynamic Qualitative Comparative Analysis Based on the TOE Framework
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly been recognized as an important driver of green innovation, yet how cities leverage AI capabilities to achieve green innovation outcomes under different configurations of conditions remains insufficiently understood. This study develops a configurational framework based on the technology–organization–environment (TOE) perspective and applies dynamic qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) to panel data from 35 Chinese cities, comprising municipalities directly under the central government, provincial capitals, and sub-provincial cities, during 2019–2023. The results identify three configurations associated with high urban green innovation. AI Technology Development and AI Institutional Support consistently emerge as core conditions across all configurations, while AI Organizational Scale is identified as a recurring peripheral condition. The findings further reveal causal asymmetry between high and non-high levels of urban green innovation, showing that individual AI-related conditions alone are insufficient to achieve high green innovation outcomes without complementary conditions. Dynamic analysis indicates that the overall configurational structures remain relatively stable over time, although the consistency of individual configurations varies as AI applications and policy environments evolve. This study advances research on AI and green innovation by demonstrating that AI-driven urban green innovation depends on the interplay among multiple conditions and involves both stable foundational factors and evolving complementary conditions.

title: Firm-Level Exposure to Climate Policy Uncertainty and Green Innovation: Nonlinear Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Climate policy uncertainty may prompt firms to prepare for regulation while delaying irreversible green investment. We examine whether firm-level exposure is nonlinearly associated with green innovation. Exposure combines a news-based provincial climate policy uncertainty index with transition exposure extracted from annual-report management discussion and analysis sections. Using 13,972 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share listed firms over 2008–2024, we estimate models with firm and year fixed effects. Green invention patent applications exhibit an inverted U-shaped association with exposure. The estimated turning point is 0.686, and 13.52% of observations exceed it; a formal U-shape test supports the pattern. R&D results are consistent with a partial internal adjustment channel, but the conditional indirect association is indistinguishable from zero in the upper exposure tail. Tighter financing constraints weaken the positive marginal association and bring forward its reversal. The curve is more pronounced among large firms, while evidence for initial asset tangibility depends on its measurement. Several robustness checks preserve the nonlinear pattern, but stricter fixed effects and province-level clustering weaken the evidence. These observational findings suggest that innovation responses depend on both policy exposure and firms’ capacity to adjust.

title: The Impact of Agency Costs on Investment Efficiency: Evidence from Overinvestment and Underinvestment in Borsa İstanbul
summary: Introduction: Agency costs can reduce resource allocation efficiency by distorting firms' investment decisions through conflicts of interest among managers, shareholders, and lenders. Therefore, examining the impact of agency costs on investment efficiency is a significant research area in the corporate finance literature. This study aims to analyze the impact of agency costs on firms' investment efficiency. Method: To determine the direction of investment inefficiency, overinvestment and underinvestment behaviors are examined through separate models. The study uses quarterly data from 24 firms listed on the BIST Industrial Index for the period 2015-2023. Investment efficiency was measured using the absolute value of residuals obtained from the expected investment model, in accordance with the approach of Biddle et al. (2009). Overinvestment and underinvestment were calculated using the positive and negative components of the residuals. Results or Findings: The study findings reveal that agency costs significantly affect investment efficiency, and this effect differs depending on the direction of investment divergence. Discussion or Conclusion: The results reval that agency costs not only increase overall investment inefficiency but can also influence both overinvestment and underinvestment behaviors of firms. These findings demonstrate that effective corporate governance mechanisms are crucial for optimizing investment decisions.

title: Step-Wise Holding Costs and Capacity Constraints in the EOQ Model: Accounting Valuation versus Operational Relevance
summary: The accuracy of the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) model relies on the validity of its input parameters, particularly the holding cost. Conventional practices often adopt a full-costing accounting approach by incorporating fixed warehousing costs (rent, depreciation, salaries) into the decision variable. This practice is reinforced by financial reporting standards IFRS (IAS 2 Inventories) and the corresponding Indonesian standard PSAK 202 (effective 2024), which require the allocation of fixed production and warehousing overheads to inventory based on normal capacity. The objective of this study is to reconstruct the EOQ holding-cost parameter by separating those fixed warehousing overheads from the relevant variable costs that should drive replenishment decisions under warehouse capacity constraints. Utilizing conceptual modelling and numerical simulation, this research proposes a reconstruction of the EOQ model using a Step-Wise Cost Function that accounts for warehouse capacity constraints. Mathematical derivation and numerical simulation demonstrate that while the financial impact of parameter errors is dampened by the model’s robustness (cost increases of 6–25%), the operational distortion is significant. The inflation of holding costs leads to a surge in ordering frequency by up to 100%, triggering logistical inefficiencies and facility congestion. This study recommends a strict decoupling of financial reporting data from operational decision-making data to mitigate these hidden operational risks.

title: Indoor environment supply chain management: Connecting digital data flow influencing sustainable development goals and knowledge dissemination
summary: This study aims to examine the impact of indoor environment, organizational culture, knowledge management, and data flow on academic library service quality within Chinese universities. It further investigates the mediating roles of supply chain integration and intellectual exports, as well as the moderating role of sustainable development goals (SDGs) orientation in strengthening service performance outcomes. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured survey administered to academic library professionals in Chinese higher education institutions. A total of 245 valid responses were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling with SmartPLS. Reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and structural relationships were assessed through bootstrapping procedures to test direct, indirect, and moderating effects. The results reveal that the indoor environment, organizational culture, knowledge management, and data flow significantly and positively influence academic library service quality. Supply chain integration and intellectual exports partially mediate these relationships. Additionally, SDGs orientation strengthens the effects of supply chain integration and intellectual exports on service quality. This study proposes and validates an integrated, multi-layered framework that combines organizational, environmental, operational, intellectual, and sustainability dimensions to explain service quality in academic libraries. The findings offer strategic insights for enhancing library performance and sustainability alignment (SDGs) in higher education institutions.

title: The Role of Ownership Structure and Real Earnings Management on the Firm Performance of Non-Financial Firms Listed in Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study investigates the impact of real earnings management (REM) on firm performance and the moderating role of ownership structure among non-financial firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Grounded in agency and stakeholder theories, the research examines how different forms of ownership specifically managerial and institutional shape the relationship between REM and firm profitability, measured through Return on Assets (ROA). Using panel data from 2008 to 2023, the study employs a dynamic panel regression model to control for firm-specific effects and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal that REM positively influences short-term profitability, but its effect is significantly moderated by ownership structure. Managerial ownership enhances overall firm performance but intensifies the negative impact of REM on ROA, suggesting potential overuse or ineffective application of REM strategies when managers hold significant equity stakes. Conversely, institutional ownership not only directly improves profitability but also weakens the positive impact of REM, reflecting its governance role in constraining opportunistic managerial behavior. These results highlight the dual influence of ownership structure in both enhancing firm performance and regulating earnings management practices. The study offers valuable insights for corporate managers, investors, and policymakers on the importance of tailoring governance mechanisms to mitigate REM risks and ensure sustainable financial performance.
